name: Office of U.S. Senator Angela Alsobrooks
subject: Senator Alsobrooks Newsletter -- September 5
body:
|

---
Dear friends and neighbors, As many of you know, I have been leading the charge to get RFK Jr. removed from his position at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). In May, I became the first U.S. Senator to call for his resignation or firing. Countless scientists at NIH in Maryland have spoken to me about his dangerous reign at HHS - halting cancer research, spreading vaccine conspiracy theories, and more. That's why yesterday, ahead of his hearing, I, along with Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), released a [54-page report](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.finance.senate.gov%2fimo%2fmedia%2fdoc%2frfk_report_203_days.pdf&redir_log=763741169003470) chronicling the devastating actions Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has taken in his first 203 days. In it, Senator Wyden and I have outlined at least one example of his costly, chaotic, and corrupt actions from each and every day he has served as Secretary. Throughout his confirmation process in the U.S. Senate, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. displayed unfitness to serve as Secretary of HHS. Nevertheless, nearly every Republican Senator fell in line, voting in favor of his nomination. Kennedy was sworn in as HHS Secretary on February 13, 2025 and Americans are now suffering the consequences each and every day. It should come as no surprise, given Kennedy's well-documented history of spreading misinformation and dangerous conspiracy theories, that his first 203 days as Secretary have been an unmitigated disaster. His actions are increasing Americans' health care costs, causing chaos, and furthering the Trump Administration's endless stream of corruption. For example:
* **Costs** : Kennedy is a key instigator of the disastrous Republican health care agenda. He helped pass Trump's budget bill, which gives massive tax handouts to the ultra-wealthy and corporations, like Big Pharma, while terminating health insurance for more than 15 million people and raising health care costs for everyone. Kennedy's purported North Star is to 'Make America Healthy Again,' but the law is diametrically opposed to that goal. The Republican budget bill will cost Americans their lives and their health coverage, while hurting their wallets.
* **Chaos** : Kennedy is systematically dismantling HHS in service of his anti-science agenda, first by decimating and threatening the critical staff and programs that keep Americans safe and healthy and second, by destabilizing the nation's gold-standard research enterprise by attacking anything contrary to his warped understanding of public health. For Kennedy, chaos and cruelty are the point - they erode public trust in the systems, institutions, research, and officials that protect the nation's wellbeing every day - allowing Kennedy to promote his dangerous vaccine pseudoscience and misinformation.
* **Corruption** : Kennedy regularly disregards the rule of law and co-opts the office of the Secretary to line the pockets of his family and his cronies. Nowhere is this pattern more apparent than in his self-serving quest to erode vaccine access nationally.

"Robert Kennedy's tenure as America's chief health officer has been higher costs, more chaos and boundless corruption," **Sen. Wyden** said. "His actions are endangering children, leaving parents confused and scared, and forcing families and taxpayers to pay more for their health care. Democrats knew from the start that Robert Kennedy would be a disastrous health secretary - it's time for Republicans to step up and hold him accountable for his actions." After the report's release, Public Citizen released the following statement: _" Public Citizen applauds Sen. Alsobrooks for shining a spotlight on Secretary Kennedy's terrible track record heading the Department of Health and Human Services. President Trump and Senate Republicans made a grievous error when entrusting Kennedy with our nation's health, with results both horrible and entirely predictable. It is far past time that President Trump rectifies this error by firing Kennedy before more lives are unnecessarily put at risk by Kennedy's anti-science views and gross mismanagement."_ Thursday morning, I appeared on [Morning Joe](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f1963577100868243532&redir_log=96771615109332) to discuss our report, as well as my renewed call for RFK Jr. to resign or be fired immediately. You can also read an article published Thursday morning in the [National Journal](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fnjour.nl%2fs%2f729485%3funlock%3d9JD2DXDAKL8ORKFI&redir_log=126607792701306), discussing our report and what's at stake for the American people. **Sick of It: Resolution Calling on RFK Jr. to Go** As you may recall, in May, I was the first Senator to call on RFK Jr. to resign or be fired as Secretary of Health and Human Services. I introduced the resolution, brought it to the floor, and my Republican colleagues objected to its passage. It was clear then, and it's crystal clear today that RFK Jr.'s decisions will cost American lives. That's why today I have reintroduced the resolution calling for his removal, and I am proud to have the support of many of my colleagues, to include: Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), and Senators Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Coons (D-Del.), Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Duckworth (D-Ill.), Heinrich (D-N.M.), Kaine (D-Va.), Kim (D-N.J.), Lujan (D-N-Mex.), Markey (D-Mass), Murray (D-Wash.), Padilla (D-Calif.), Reed (D-R.I.), Rosen (D-Nev.), Sanders (D-Vt.), Schiff (D-Calif.), Smith (D-Minn.),Warren (D-Mass.), Warner (D-Va.), Warnock (D-Ga.), Welch (D-Vt.), and Van Hollen (D-Md.). I will not stop until Secretary Kennedy resigns or is removed from office. You can read the resolution [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.alsobrooks.senate.gov%2fwp-content%2fuploads%2f2025%2f09%2fRFKFINAL-PDF.pdf&redir_log=235386137412498).
**Health Care: A Moral Issue** Health care is a moral issue and a human right. If you're in the Baltimore area tomorrow, join us for a powerful community forum that will explore the impact of federal health care cuts and how we can fight back. RSVP [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fdocs.google.com%2fforms%2fd%2f1LqHTONi3GfT-D8EbhNHK5E8pXvM3ZeiKqiDoWq75lsw%2fviewform%3fedit_requested%3dtrue&redir_log=776862213304724). [](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fdocs.google.com%2fforms%2fd%2f1LqHTONi3GfT-D8EbhNHK5E8pXvM3ZeiKqiDoWq75lsw%2fviewform%3fedit_requested%3dtrue&redir_log=776862213304724)
**In the Community** As you may be aware, the Senate has just returned from the August work period, and I was pleased to have the opportunity to visit with Marylanders from the Eastern Shore to Western Maryland. Here are some of the stops we made along the way. ********* I had such a great time enjoying crabs at Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity, Inc. Zeta Sigma Chapter's 40th Annual Crab Feast in Baltimore! During these challenging times in our country, I am grateful to surround myself with love, joy, and community. I was glad to meet with Eastern Shore business community leaders to learn more about their challenges and victories. It is absolutely essential for me to hear from all Marylanders. I represent Maryland best when I am fighting for what you need. It was such a joy to meet with seniors - and young children - at the Chesapeake Grove Intergenerational Center. This beautiful center cares for young children and creates a community for our seniors. I assured the seniors I will always work to protect them. Health care workers care for everyone - illness does not discriminate. But now health care workers are spending precious time worrying about cuts to Medicaid and rural health care. I am grateful to have heard directly from health care leaders from the Eastern Shore region. I was honored to attend the National Organization of Black Women in Law Enforcement's 40th Annual Scholarship Luncheon and applaud them for 40 years of making a difference. On a beautiful Maryland day, I loved touring and walking around Westminster's Main Street. Thank you to Westminster Mayor Mona Becker for welcoming me to visit and learn more about the ways you continue to work to grow local business. I can't wait to visit again soon. I was glad to meet with Westminster's Downtown Business Association and assured them that I am fighting back to protect our businesses and lower costs. This business community goes above and beyond to support one another, and ensure that Westminster has a thriving economy. Thank you, Frederick, for welcoming Congresswoman McClain Delaney and me! We loved taking your questions and hearing your concerns. Let's stay encouraged, and let's encourage each other. We are going to make it through this time. Together. See a recap of the [Community Conversation here.](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f1961521886082261378&redir_log=357915758536333) Absolutely loved my lunch at JeannieBird Baking Company in Westminster! Their food was fantastic. Thanks for having me - I will be back! Fibroids impact 80% of women yet only 0.03% of our research dollars go to studying it. I sat down with women's health providers at Frederick Health to discuss how my U-FIGHT Act will fight for fibroid research, and how we can ensure access to women's health care in Western Maryland.
**Delivering for You** Our office has been working hard to deliver for Marylanders, and I'm happy to share a few success stories from our constituent services team over the last week.
* Successfully worked to ensure constituents were able to receive their Social Security benefits.
* Helped a constituent receive $8,500 back from the IRS.
* Resolved 118 constituent requests for information and questions regarding federal agencies.

Our constituent services team stands ready to assist you! If you are a veteran who needs help navigating the Department of Veterans Affairs, if you're having trouble navigating Social Security, the IRS or immigration, please reach out to our team by filling out the applicable form [here](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.alsobrooks.senate.gov%2fservices%2fcasework%2f&redir_log=48139330565369). **Stay Informed** I know these are difficult times. But please know that I will continue fighting for you every step of the way. We will not give up. We will not give in to this Administration, and I ask that you continue to fight alongside us. Please continue to reach out to us. You can call the office, connect with us, or find resources for those who have been laid off at [alsobrooks.senate.gov](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15361.11464064.5623520.7190525&report_id=&redirect=http%3a%2f%2falsobrooks.senate.gov&redir_log=983830187668200). You can also follow us on Bluesky, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, and X. We are in this TOGETHER. Sincerely, Angela D. Alsobrooks

In May, I became the first U.S. Senator to call for his resignation or firing. Countless scientists at NIH in Maryland have spoken to me about his dangerous reign at HHS - halting cancer research, spreading vaccine conspiracy theories, and more. That's why yesterday, ahead of his hearing, I, along with Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), released a chronicling the devastating actions Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has taken in his first 203 days. In it, Senator Wyden and I have outlined at least one example of his costly, chaotic, and corrupt actions from each and every day he has served as Secretary. Throughout his confirmation process in the U.S. Senate, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. displayed unfitness to serve as Secretary of HHS. Nevertheless, nearly every Republican Senator fell in line, voting in favor of his nomination. Kennedy was sworn in as HHS Secretary on February 13, 2025 and Americans are now suffering the consequences each and every day. It should come as no surprise, given Kennedy's well-documented history of spreading misinformation and dangerous conspiracy theories, that his first 203 days as Secretary have been an unmitigated disaster. His actions are increasing Americans' health care costs, causing chaos, and furthering the Trump Administration's endless stream of corruption. For example: Costs : Kennedy is a key instigator of the disastrous Republican health care agenda. He helped pass Trump's budget bill, which gives massive tax handouts to the ultra-wealthy and corporations, like Big Pharma, while terminating health insurance for more than 15 million people and raising health care costs for everyone. Kennedy's purported North Star is to 'Make America Healthy Again,' but the law is diametrically opposed to that goal. The Republican budget bill will cost Americans their lives and their health coverage, while hurting their wallets. body:
You should see this

Folks,
The support from people in California and across the country for the Election Rigging Response Act has been absolutely overwhelming.
We've received more than 500,000 individual donations in just a few weeks. It means the world to Governor Newsom.
And it's a good thing, because we're going up against $100 million in opposition spending. No, that is not a typo. One guy alone who loves giving to extreme causes and candidates has already given $20 million to beat us.
But because of your support, we thought it important to take a second and pull back the curtain on what we are doing with the donations.
In the year 2025, you can no longer just put one ad on TV and hope to win. People are consuming information and entertainment on broadcast, on cable, on YouTube, on Facebook, Hulu and on and on it goes.
This campaign has one message: Stop Donald Trump from rigging the 2026 election before a single vote is cast. But we deliver it on different platforms, with different messengers.
Here are a few examples of ads we've created and are running.
Direct from Governor Newsom.
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/4770?t=1&akid=2517%2E4767699%2EzJljBc)
Senator Alex Padilla
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/4771?t=2&akid=2517%2E4767699%2EzJljBc)
A bit more direct on Trump.
[](https://act.gavinnewsom.com/go/4773?t=3&akid=2517%2E4767699%2EzJljBc)
The truth is - people hate what Donald Trump is doing in Texas. Republicans, Democrats, and Independents alike. They just want a level playing field where ideas are debated and people vote.
That's what the Election Rigging Response Act does. And it's why we'll win if we have the resources to reach our voters and persuadable voters in the different places they are watching "television" these days.
Thank you,
Team Newsom
* * *
i️ To my fellow Democrats — don't scroll past this. 🇺🇸
I have heard the calls do "Do something!" and I agree. If Texas wants to redraw their maps, California will fight fire with fire.
God help us if we're not successful. We may have enjoyed our last free and fair election. They're redrawing districts to hold the House; going after ActBlue and Democrats' ability to fundraise; going after colleges and the free press... We have to act.
[**Please make a contribution to help us get it done. The amount isn't as important as the donation itself. I need to know you're with me as we press forward.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/erra-em?refcode=em250903&refcode2=2517_4767699_zJljBc&akid=2517%2E4767699%2EzJljBc)

#### Teichert in the Trenches - September 2025
Welcome to this month’s installment of Teichert in the Trenches, a monthly newsletter highlighting a snippet of my attempts to maximize my impact on people and our great nation and to develop the leaders our nation needs! In the My Bookshelf section below, check out the pre-order special from my friend Leland Vittert and his upcoming book entitled Born Lucky! ** _Teichert in the News_**

---
Midshipman Noah Teichert (he’s in the back) taking his oath of office as he starts Navy ROTC at Vanderbilt. This is actually the third time he’s taken the oath (IYKYK), though he’s still 17 years old. We are very proud of him, and his willingness to serve our great nation.
| | | |
---
And check out those shiny boots!
|

📕 I am thrilled to announce that a new book is in the works that will be a perfect contribution to our nation’s 250th Birthday in 2026. It should be out shortly after the new year.💥 Pastor Brad Wells (GraceWay Baptist Church in Washington, DC) and I did our first planning session last week after a bit of time praying over our great nation from the U.S. Capitol! We are busy reflecting on and writing about our nation's historic dependency on God and the current necessity of making our national motto our personal declaration.
**_My Bookshelf_**
|
---
| [ Order "Born Lucky" here](https://eufi5.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/SMK1E8tHeGZMVG1nXO576ihZNedE/rucxooRqZnnj)
---
I’ve had the privilege of joining Leland (aka Lucky) several times on his primetime show on NewsNation, and have been blessed to get to know him on and off set. His book is a powerful one – a touching and applicable story of a struggling young person who finds a pathway to turn daunting challenges into incredible opportunities (it truly reminds me of a modern-day version of Teddy Roosevelt). “Dad’s only real rule for me, his ultimate lesson, was this: You don’t have to be defined by a diagnosis. You get to decide who you are. The message is powerful because it applies to everyone. It doesn’t matter if you’re on the spectrum, have a physical disability, struggle with anxiety, a speech impediment, or a cleft palate – whatever challenge you face, it doesn’t have to define you. What matters is defining yourself on your terms, no matter what the world wants to call you. It sounds hokey, but it’s true. The flip side is also true: If you let it define you ... it will, forever.” I strongly recommend you Pre-Order a Copy today at the link above! Or, through midnight tonight you can order it for 25% off here: https://www.barnesandnoble.com/w/born-lucky-leland-vittert/1147108657
|
---
“The irony across all self-protection is that at the same time as we’re worrying about machine learning and artificial intelligence taking jobs and dehumanizing work, we’re intentionally or unintentionally creating cultures that, instead of leveraging the unique gifts of the human heart like vulnerability, empathy, and emotional literacy, are trying to lock those gifts away.”
|
---
“We often (or even usually) know what we should be doing in both personal and professional life. We also know why we should be doing it and (often) how to do it. Figuring all that out is not too difficult. What is very hard is actually doing what you know to be god for you in the long-run, in spite of short-run temptations. The same is true for organizations ... Just because something is obvious doesn’t make it easy. Real strategy lies not in figuring out what to do, but in devising ways to ensure that, compared to others, we actually do more of what everybody knows they should do.”
|
---
“For transformative change to be sustainable, it not only has to take root in its own culture, but also has to successfully engage its changing environment. It must be adaptive to both internal and external realities. Therefore, leadership needs to start with listening and learning, finding out where people are, valuing what is best in what they already know, value, and do, and build from there. It’s dangerous to lead with only a change idea in mind. You need both a healthy respect for the values, competence, and history of people, as well as the changing environment, to build the capacity to respond to new challenges and take advantage of new openings.”
|
---
“Every age has had its crusaders – men like Mitchell whose relentless insistence on the correctness of their beliefs ultimately destroyed them. In the interim, however, their zeal also sustained them in combating the antagonism of the shortsighted ... Americans might well regard Mitchell as one of the extraordinary men in their history, one who employed some remarkable gifts and usual energy in trying to alert his countrymen to the promise of aviation.”
|
---
“Air power in the future will be a determining factor in international competitions, both military and civil. American characteristics and temperament are particularly suitable to its development.” ** _PLUS Posts for the Month_**

💥🔥 Owning it from her earliest days!

🏫 🎒 While Tiffany starts her senior year at TCU this next week, she’s been owning it for a long while now. This was her popping into my office when I was a squadron commander and taking over the place. It’s a trend item wherever she goes and whatever she does!

🐸 Go Frogs and Go Tiffany!
| | |

| |

| | | As we approach the anniversary of 9/11, I always think about the experience of doing the Memorial Stair Climb in 2017. Chief Michael Perry and I joined our first responder team from Joint Base Andrews to climb 110 stories in full firefighter gear. It was a grueling experience and gave me an extra dose of appreciation for our community heroes!
---

Copyrighted song lyrics from my Middle School Days!

🎶 I wrote the following in Middle School as a bit of a riff off of "Born in the USA." Then, I successfully pursued a copyright for it. There is certainly enough in here to make you laugh while maybe telegraphing my future focus on national security and international affairs.

🔥 If you ask me nicely in person, I might even sing it for you. In other contexts, I’ve been told that “You’ve got bars!” -- whatever that means. 🤣 ** _Rejoin Opportunities_**

Prayer Breakfast](https://eufi5.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsEcDi1QiaMFOpU26ddzgW/Ad8IShyX9Cl-)
---
If you are in the northwest Arkansas region on the morning of September 12th, it would be wonderful to have you join us at the Annual Fort Smith Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast where I’ll be providing the keynote speech.
|
---
Also, if you are in the Washington, D.C. area at 10am on September 16th, I’ll be speaking at the Air Force Memorial about the legacy of Billy Mitchell to celebrate the Air Force Birthday Week. It would be great to see you there, and the biggest reason why you probably noticed two books about Billy Mitchell on my reading list this month. ** _Dad Joke of the Month_** Did you know that someone is forming a flight company that caters to bald customers? They’re calling it Receding Airlines.

My Bookshelf | | I’ve had the privilege of joining Leland (aka Lucky) several times on his primetime show on NewsNation, and have been blessed to get to know him on and off set. His book is a powerful one – a touching and applicable story of a struggling young person who finds a pathway to turn daunting challenges into incredible opportunities (it truly reminds me of a modern-day version of Teddy Roosevelt). “Dad’s only real rule for me, his ultimate lesson, was this: You don’t have to be defined by a diagnosis. You get to decide who you are. The message is powerful because it applies to everyone. It doesn’t matter if you’re on the spectrum, have a physical disability, struggle with anxiety, a speech impediment, or a cleft palate – whatever challenge you face, it doesn’t have to define you. What matters is defining yourself on your terms, no matter what the world wants to call you. It sounds hokey, but it’s true. The flip side is also true: If you let it define you ... it will, forever.” I strongly recommend you Pre-Order a Copy today at the link above! Or, through midnight tonight you can order it for 25% off here: | “The irony across all self-protection is that at the same time as we’re worrying about machine learning and artificial intelligence taking jobs and dehumanizing work, we’re intentionally or unintentionally creating cultures that, instead of leveraging the unique gifts of the human heart like vulnerability, empathy, and emotional literacy, are trying to lock those gifts away.” | “We often (or even usually) know what we should be doing in both personal and professional life. We also know why we should be doing it and (often) how to do it. Figuring all that out is not too difficult. What is very hard is actually doing what you know to be god for you in the long-run, in spite of short-run temptations. The same is true for organizations ... Just because something is obvious doesn’t make it easy. Real strategy lies not in figuring out what to do, but in devising ways to ensure that, compared to others, we actually do more of what everybody knows they should do.” | “For transformative change to be sustainable, it not only has to take root in its own culture, but also has to successfully engage its changing environment. It must be adaptive to both internal and external realities. Therefore, leadership needs to start with listening and learning, finding out where people are, valuing what is best in what they already know, value, and do, and build from there. It’s dangerous to lead with only a change idea in mind. You need both a healthy respect for the values, competence, and history of people, as well as the changing environment, to build the capacity to respond to new challenges and take advantage of new openings.” | “Every age has had its crusaders – men like Mitchell whose relentless insistence on the correctness of their beliefs ultimately destroyed them. In the interim, however, their zeal also sustained them in combating the antagonism of the shortsighted ... Americans might well regard Mitchell as one of the extraordinary men in their history, one who employed some remarkable gifts and usual energy in trying to alert his countrymen to the promise of aviation.” | “Air power in the future will be a determining factor in international competitions, both military and civil. American characteristics and temperament are particularly suitable to its development.” PLUS Posts for the Month | | | | | "Pronouns Matter" | "Finding the Stars" | "We Must Listen" | "Transforming Common Days into Thanksgiving" | | | Blasts from the Past | | | | | 💥🔥 Owning it from her earliest days! 🏫 🎒 While Tiffany starts her senior year at TCU this next week, she’s been owning it for a long while now. This was her popping into my office when I was a squadron commander and taking over the place. It’s a trend item wherever she goes and whatever she does! 🐸 Go Frogs and Go Tiffany! | | | | | | | | As we approach the anniversary of 9/11, I always think about the experience of doing the Memorial Stair Climb in 2017. Chief Michael Perry and I joined our first responder team from Joint Base Andrews to climb 110 stories in full firefighter gear. It was a grueling experience and gave me an extra dose of appreciation for our community heroes! | | | | Copyrighted song lyrics from my Middle School Days! 🎶 I wrote the following in Middle School as a bit of a riff off of "Born in the USA." Then, I successfully pursued a copyright for it. There is certainly enough in here to make you laugh while maybe telegraphing my future focus on national security and international affairs. 🔥 If you ask me nicely in person, I might even sing it for you. In other contexts, I’ve been told that “You’ve got bars!” -- whatever that means. 🤣 Rejoin Opportunities | - If you are in the northwest Arkansas region on the morning of September 12th, it would be wonderful to have you join us at the Annual Fort Smith Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast where I’ll be providing the keynote speech. | Also, if you are in the Washington, D.C. area at 10am on September 16th, I’ll be speaking at the Air Force Memorial about the legacy of Billy Mitchell to celebrate the Air Force Birthday Week. It would be great to see you there, and the biggest reason why you probably noticed two books about Billy Mitchell on my reading list this month. | Peter, Trump’s henchmen showed up on our streets. At job sites. In our neighborhoods. In early May, nearly 200 of our neighbors in South Nashville were rounded up in a sweeping ICE raid — a federal operation that had the blessing and cooperation of Bill Lee and Tennessee Republicans. They call it law and order. But here’s the truth: **📊 65% of people detained by ICE this year had no criminal convictions.
📊 93% had never been convicted of a violent offense.** ** ** Most of those detained are not and have never been threats to public safety. They are parents. They are workers. They are Tennesseans trying to build a better life for their families. This is what Trump’s assault on innocent immigrants looks like: indiscriminate arrests, no due process, shattered families, and fear flooding our communities — all while DHS admits it can only name _four_ people with criminal records out of the nearly 200 taken in Nashville. **The Tennessee House Democratic Caucus is fighting back.** We’ve introduced legislation to protect immigrant families, promote local control over policing, and ensure due process for every Tennessean — regardless of status. But we need your help. 👉 Can you chip in $20 to power our fight for humane, practical immigration policy?

# Trump DOJ considering transgender gun ban
The Trump Justice Department is reportedly considering **[blocking transgender individuals from purchasing firearms,](https://substack.com/redirect/e9572db0-de26-498e-bde8-cf9fb2da0ae3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with sources citing gender dysphoria as a mental disorder that could make individuals "unstable and unwell" when obtaining weapons.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/df20305e-88be-4a4d-87a1-ea5613eb6324?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Recent Shooting Context:** The discussions follow the Minneapolis Catholic school shooting by Robin Westman, a transgender woman who killed two children, which occurred two years after the Nashville Covenant School shooting by another transgender individual, prompting calls to investigate "transgender domestic terrorism."
* **Political Divide:** While Republicans argue for examining warning signs in transgender shooters and implementing such restrictions as "common sense," Democrats like Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey have criticized directing "hate" toward the transgender community and warned against villainizing any group after these incidents.
* **Broader Policy Context:** The potential firearm restrictions contrast sharply with Minnesota Governor Tim Walz's approach of establishing the state as a "trans refuge" and protecting access to gender-affirming care, while he separately calls for addressing gun violence through reducing access to firearms generally.

# Trump sarcastically jabs India for cozying up to America's "deepest, darkest" enemies
President Trump expressed frustration on Truth Social about India and Russia's growing ties with China, **[sarcastically commenting](https://substack.com/redirect/7d6861b9-ea19-4e45-a0d2-75845d29ad09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** "Looks like we've lost India and Russia to deepest, darkest, China" and wishing them "a long and prosperous future together."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7d6861b9-ea19-4e45-a0d2-75845d29ad09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Military Parade Appearance:** The criticism followed a public appearance by Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at a military parade in Beijing commemorating the 80th anniversary of WWII's end.
* **Trump's Interpretation:** Trump characterized the joint appearance as the leaders "conspiring against the US" and suggested China's military display was specifically intended for his attention, saying "they were hoping I was watching -- and I was watching."
* **Economic Pressure on India:** The comments come after Trump imposed 50% tariffs on Indian goods and publicly criticized New Delhi for what his administration views as opportunistic purchases of cheap Russian oil, demonstrating escalating tensions with India over its foreign policy choices.

body:
Hear from digital economy experts in this virtual panel

| | | | | |
---
|

[|

|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **Virtual Panel: AI's Emerging Workforce Impact** _On Sept. 11, hear from digital economy experts Erik Brynjolfsson and Bharat Chandar of Stanford’s Digital Economy Lab_
On Thursday, September 11, join a [virtual panel](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=8adcaab808&e=a07d75591f) with digital economy experts Erik Brynjolfsson and Bharat Chandar to discuss the impact of artificial intelligence on the jobs landscape. Following a jobs report that indicates a [national slow-down](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=a3d71e13d4&e=a07d75591f) in hiring, the panel will discuss Brynjolfsson and Chandar’s [recent research](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=4857bf3fb0&e=a07d75591f), which finds clear evidence of AI’s impact on jobs for entry-level workers.
**Register for the Virtual Panel:**[**AI’s Emerging Workforce Impact**](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=866e04b2d5&e=a07d75591f)

---
[|
---](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=6b300ec561&e=a07d75591f)
| | **AI’s Emerging Workforce Impact** Thursday, September 11, 202512:00PM ET[**RSVP here**](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=dcee211cbe&e=a07d75591f)**.**
This August, Brynjolfsson and Chandar released new [research](https://responsibleinnovation.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c0dd7c48fa7fb81cbc8185a&id=6b03de74ac&e=a07d75591f) titled _Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence_. The report examines changes in the labor market for occupations exposed to AI using high-frequency administrative data from the largest payroll software provider in the United States. The paper finds that since the widespread adoption of AI, early-career workers (ages 22-25) in the most exposed occupations have experienced a 13 percent relative decline in employment even after controlling for firm-level shocks.

| | | Friends,On Monday, Judge Amit Mehta, who has already found Google to be an illegal monopolist, issued a long, seemingly elegant opinion that explains why Google's moat building and controlling conduct is a problem. And then he largely concluded there's not much to be done about it, though he cloaks it in enough language that you might think there's muscle there. The government said Google should be forced to divest Chrome or Android. Mehta called that too risky and messy. Sure, he barred exclusive default-placement deals, but astonishingly allowed Google to still pay billions to keep prime placement on Apple devices. He ordered some data-sharing with rivals, but not the crown jewels of ad data. Alphabet's stock jumped, because through all the thicket of words, the essence was clear: go on monopolizing, Google. Data monarchs are safer. If you were mad when SCOTUS gave POTUS immunity, you should be furious when Judge Mehta recognizes lawbreaking and then shrugs, because using the obvious remedy would be too messy. The dangers of concentrated power in data have never been greater. Defaults are critically important during the growth of AI, but if Mehta's ruling stands, Google, which already filters and sorts what we see and hear, and is racing to dominate AI, got told to tidy up its contracts and share a bit of data but keep on with its power hoarding. That's how unaccountable power compounds.This summer, I found myself struggling to follow the news, because so much of it felt like bad entertainment. There's too much talk of crisis in terms of personality, the personality of Trump, the personality of his henchmen, the personality of MAGA. There's an effort to make all of these monsters, ogres, outside, other, alien, invaders on a safe comfortable world. But they are results of concentration of power, not weird invaders. The root issue today is too much concentrated power, and unless we confront it, we can't confront the corruption that is rotting our democracy. Too much power in the Presidency, which allows the corruption of Congress, too much power in the federal government, which allows the enervation of local democracy, and far, far too much power in a few big AI companies, building off their power in data and advertising technology. We allow that power to isolate and dominate. And if we refuse to confront the structures of power, we'll keep manufacturing new monsters, and we'll have a lots of fairy tales, but not the change we need. What if, instead of fretting about the "messiness" of breaking up a monarch, the court embraced the older American wisdom Justice William O. Douglas articulated in 1948:
> "For all power tends to develop into a government in itself. Power that controls the economy should be in the hands of elected representatives of the people, not in the hands of an industrial oligarchy. Industrial power should be decentralized--scattered into many hands--so that the fortunes of the people will not be dependent on the whim or caprice...of a few self-appointed men."
Clinging to cloaks of legalism instead of confronting power, that's a bad habit recently among Democratic Party elites too. There are plenty of anti-Trumpers who like the concentration so long as their side holds it. But refusing to directly address power is bad for democracy and bad politics. Seeing the problem as one of power means we don't just gripe about SCOTUS and POTUS; we also call out legal gymnastics--like this week's Google ruling--and demand structural remedies: breakups, neutral-platform rules, and campaign-finance reform, more experiments in local democracy, more energy at the city and state level, less nervousness around the data oligarchs. More soon,--Zephyr[Support this newsletter](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/935ae2b4?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)I was away for the summer, working on longer writing projects and [doing some theater](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/558f653f?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21). Hope to write more now!

Hi Peter,

It was a busy summer at Her Bold Move, and in our country as a whole. We wanted to send you a quick summary of what you may have missed as it pertains to our work:
* We saw some bizarre headlines, like CNN’s profile of a pastor named Douglas Wilson and the influential movement he leads. **The piece explained that his movement preaches that women should not be allowed to _vote_ or hold leadership positions. **

**It was later revealed that members of the Trump administration are congregants of this church, and hold this dangerously sexist worldview as well...**
* Another headline came from Tennessee, where a 35-year-old pregnant woman was denied prenatal care by her physician because she was “unwed.” This type of formerly illegal discrimination has now been deemed legal in TN.
* In Colorado, a state Representative snapped a photo of his female colleague, another state lawmaker, without her knowledge or permission. Within an hour, the photo ended up on an “anonymous social media account with conservative followers” with the caption “Smash or Pass,” and the photo has continued to circulate online.
* We also saw the passing and signing of Donald Trump’s “Big Beautiful Bill.” The lack of women’s representation in the room where that bill was being written was abundantly clear as it explicitly stripped access to healthcare away from millions of people – and will have an outsized impact on American women.

[**If you’ve been away from the news this summer, we’re glad you’re back. But the reality is, we need you now more than ever. Donald Trump and his allies are aggressively rolling back women’s rights – and our best defense will be to have as many women in government as possible to block their efforts. On that note, here’s some much-needed GOOD NEWS:
* Her Bold Move spent the summer endorsing and supporting qualified women candidates across the country. We even added our first candidate from Utah, which means Her Bold Move has worked in 43 states + 1 U.S. territory since we started doing this work 5 years ago. We can’t wait to hit all 50 in the coming year!
* We have achieved a 100% win rate in the 2025 primaries, a truly remarkable accomplishment that fills us with pride. Despite some extremely challenging races and formidable opponents, our candidates have ALL managed to emerge from the primary season victorious – [**rush $20.26 right now to help these candidates prepare for the General election this November. →**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hbm-pac/?refcode=EM_F_250906ICYMI_N_HBM_90DO_13_NG_N_L2&amount=20.26)

Oh, and Taylor Swift got engaged in case you missed that. :)

Our mission here at Her Bold Move is as clear as ever – we need to elect women into rooms where decisions are being made. The anti-woman movement is growing more and more powerful every day, and Her Bold Move is on the front line of the pushback. We know exactly what we need to do to fight back.

Florida’s surgeon general, Joseph Ladapo, stood next to the governor and[ said the state would move to end every vaccine mandate](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=a33f9da127f36a73bb4aa9b66249ff4c16dc4e317e3c2bdeb9a93e44c9f02849&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=9cb14afcaf12cdfe3dab777e6ce3f7ec&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYm1qLmNvbS9jb250ZW50LzM5MC9ibWoucjE4NzAuZnVsbA=&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30) it can — starting with school requirements for diseases like measles and polio — casting mandates as an assault on “bodily autonomy.”
But removing vaccine mandates would require the Florida legislature to change[ current statutes](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=bf15408974544088d96ac97c335ffc322e79f097ea79315efa8c8c9d7fc87938&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=f247a94bbf4339f28275ea2b435040b7&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubGVnLnN0YXRlLmZsLnVzL3N0YXR1dGVzL2luZGV4LmNmbT9BcHBfbW9kZT1EaXNwbGF5X1N0YXR1dGUmVVJMPTEwMDAtMTA5OS8xMDAzL1NlY3Rpb25zLzEwMDMuMjIuaHRtbA=&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30), and that’s not something the legislature is ready or willing to do, three representatives told me today.
“Hard pass,” a Republican state house member told me over text messages.
“Even the White House isn’t on board with this for now,” said another.
And today, Senator Rick Scott[ openly opposed](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=ae1887cf50cbb5a8b22a0aa64a7cf5c771ff135dd6491d5f3cb5e42d309e63c8&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=ffcc2eb6521770b5e9da7a8ebb65722b&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tL2xvY2FsL3RhbXBhLWJheS8yMDI1LzA5LzA0L3JpY2stc2NvdHQtcm9uLWRlc2FudGlzLWZsb3JpZGEtdmFjY2luZS1tYW5kYXRlcw=&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30) the push to remove mandates.
"Florida already has a good system that allows families to opt out based on religious and personal beliefs, which balances our children's health and parents' rights," Scott told Axios.
That immediate pushback has already resulted in vague threats from Ladapo.
"People are going to have to choose a side,” [Ladapo said](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=689b47967404777888a9f5bebeb81577ebb36453701f0ea107d8b05e143fcd40&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=4f620b2be6207cbf5e0d3dbd808202d1&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cucmV1dGVycy5jb20vYnVzaW5lc3MvaGVhbHRoY2FyZS1waGFybWFjZXV0aWNhbHMvZmxvcmlkYS1wbGFuLWVuZC12YWNjaW5lLW1hbmRhdGVzLXdpbGwtZmFjZS1jaGFsbGVuZ2VzLXN0YXRlLWxlZ2lzbGF0dXJlLTIwMjUtMDktMDUv&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30).
[Click here to subscribe](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=796f876f8911462f923659ce122fd49ef058cad880eb61ada2c0575ac9962468&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=1b8a184902d8152a380307c31f2b9bbf&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubWVzb3NjYWxlbmV3cy5jb20vc3Vic2NyaWJl&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30)
Florida has already fallen below target in vaccination rates, and recent outbreaks of measles bring the risk to the forefront of concern.
“All it takes is one child traveling to an endemic country and coming back to school with measles. Or going to a state with a live outbreak,” said Dorit Reiss, a University of California Law Professor who specializes in vaccine law.
“Vaccine mandates did not always exist in all states, but part of the reason of the move to all states having them in the 1980s was data showing mandates reduce outbreaks,” said Reiss.
“We may be going back to a natural experiment where some states will see more outbreaks as their laws weaken,” Reiss added.
Pressure coming from HHS in Idaho, [West Virginia](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=e7abef50a1516b9d80e8ff1cbba025f23a7ffe1e7acfe0924692e40473d0c6cf&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=f8d2abea4f1a8eb6a86f6e095d86f806&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaGhzLmdvdi9zaXRlcy9kZWZhdWx0L2ZpbGVzL2RjLWxldHRlci13dmhkLXZhY2NpbmVzLWNoaWxkcmVuLXByb2dyYW0ucGRm&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30) and Texas may lead other Republican-controlled states to weaken laws, as well.
[Click here to subscribe](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=796f876f8911462f923659ce122fd49ef058cad880eb61ada2c0575ac9962468&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=1b8a184902d8152a380307c31f2b9bbf&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubWVzb3NjYWxlbmV3cy5jb20vc3Vic2NyaWJl&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30)
One potential hold out is Mississippi, which has one of the strictest vaccine laws in the country with no allowance for religious or philosophical exemptions, and consequently[ one of the highest compliance rate](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=e4d264b647a615926d718a86a8315906341cc1136bfc1016cc945fc3f9d477ee&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=109fd33fafa96a5b8d3154fce0768eef&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY2RjLmdvdi9zY2hvb2x2YXh2aWV3L2RhdGEvaW5kZXguaHRtbA=&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30)s in the country.
“I strongly doubt that [Mississippi] would ever do anything like Florida,” said Dr. Justin Turner, former Chief Medical Officer for the Mississippi Department of Health. “I can see [Surgeon General] Dr. Edney dying on that hill.”
[](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=453f666d75b8c92e051ca917a5ba68963f751c91acde0c5d67fa46b901468e2d&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=84e9a381ea8deda20ef3247b7b67e6e0&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zdWJzdGFja2Nkbi5jb20vaW1hZ2UvZmV0Y2gvJTI0c18heWJyciEsZl9hdXRvLHFfYXV0bzpnb29kLGZsX3Byb2dyZXNzaXZlOnN0ZWVwL2h0dHBzJTNBJTJGJTJGc3Vic3RhY2stcG9zdC1tZWRpYS5zMy5hbWF6b25hd3MuY29tJTJGcHVibGljJTJGaW1hZ2VzJTJGNGQwODM2NjQtODY1Zi00N2I5LWJiZjQtZTZhMmZhOWEwZTQ3XzE4MDh4MTEyNS5wbmc&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30)
Florida’s debate is likely to continue in the months ahead, with lawmakers, health officials, and families weighing in on the balance between DeSantis’ fear-mongering and public health and safety.
The stakes are immediate: with vaccination coverage already sliding and measles outbreaks appearing across the country, the dismantling of Florida’s mandates could accelerate a return to the kinds of epidemics parents and doctors thought were long behind us.
[Click here to subscribe](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=796f876f8911462f923659ce122fd49ef058cad880eb61ada2c0575ac9962468&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=1b8a184902d8152a380307c31f2b9bbf&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubWVzb3NjYWxlbmV3cy5jb20vc3Vic2NyaWJl&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30)
Whether legislators hold the line or cave to political pressure, the consequences will be measured not in votes but in infections.
[Click here to find your Florida legislators and tell them NO to removing mandates.](https://geojones2.wordpress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=ef4f7cf212db316fa186432ba0bfade791e3155c7febb83cefc7e17d477b687e&blog_id=26166017&post_id=3664&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=31270d533e930acb6a14b112f4778545&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZmxob3VzZS5nb3YvRmluZFlvdXJSZXByZXNlbnRhdGl2ZQ=&email_id=4804bd8fc64a8ab4d270751416721b30)

body:
Only somebody who dodged the draft five times and let somebody else go in his place would want to command the Department of War.
#
Peter —
Let us remind you, though at this point you already know.
Donald Trump never served. Never wore the uniform. Matter of fact, he did everything he could to avoid serving. Dodged the draft multiple times, a real Fortunate Son. Even called dodging STDs in the 80s his personal Vietnam. That matters today, and here’s why:
World War Two was the deadliest war in human history. Nearly 100 million people were killed, civilian and military. War is hell, and after World War Two people started to recognize that war should only be waged as a last resort.
American leaders, both civilian and military, named the Department of War the Department of Defense because they recognized the truth — war is hell. Defense, not war, should be our priority.
But Trump’s an idiot, a coward with soft hands and a silver spoon. Only somebody who dodged the draft five times and let somebody else go in his place would want to command the Department of War.
It might sound insignificant with everything else happening, but this kind of thing is still important. It’s about how this nation perceives itself and is perceived by the world. Project strength, prioritize peace, and resort to war when you have no other option.
As long as we have breath in our lungs, VoteVets is going to fight this. Changing the name of the Department of Defense requires an act of Congress, and we’ll fight like hell to make sure that act never passes.
Peter, we need your help to rally our allies, mobilize Veterans around the country, and stop this.

clean_body: Get the Moms for America Opt-Out form. Every mom deserves to know her rights. Every child deserves to be protected. If you are having trouble viewing this email click here to view in your browser. [] [] * Together, we can stop this agenda in its tracks and defend the future of our children! [] [] Moms, we must take a stand. Schools are pushing mental health screenings that invade our children’s privacy and undermine parental authority. That’s why we’ve created this opt-out form, a simple way for parents to say NO to government overreach and keep control where it belongs: with moms and dads. Watch this short video to see what’s happening in Illinois – and why it’s coming to a state near you if we don’t act now. Download and fill out the Opt-Out Form to protect your child today. But we need your help to get this in the hands of every parent. Will you join us today with just $3? One dollar for each point in our fight. | | | Peter, We’ve got a LOT of exciting news to share from the past month, so we put together this WFP newsletter just for you! Keep reading to catch up on our recent wins and updates for the fight ahead.
* * *
**_Notching More WFP Victories!_** If you thought this year’s Working Families Party wave was just in New York City – _think again_. Working Families Party candidates scored primary wins from Seattle to Detroit to Tucson this past month. Wins like these are only possible because of WFP members like you who donate their time, energy, and resources to electing champions for working people at every level of government, and taking the fight directly to the billionaires. [**See the full recap of our primary season wins here.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYd6eLP33O2GRZpvuK-wGuQ8xFrrzufE3qFooru6OnHRFIELElv3Xqskop-fwi87Eu88AFt38FYeTwutfjdn-2meuev20mc5WNpoVxhu-OwucJIAT1HwEUWWW4_O_UYfXEDV9LQYWhCuQnhwrMxKdP5bq6oF4WEK6TM6xyjSf_8BnfFgKUXzLKazg_8p9ooVGWxYI8sUK4OItJ2qRVP85xqjEDa5NzYBOflKirIJGqvuU7t8AZQiHfgslxzVr1d_5xgLoe1gVAxp0QCjTSPPoMHxOM5JE4Fu7hf2bEFyS8fYCY742Qgo__4CvOPL16q5A4g0EEWSzDky6IUaEbhFVvqjhOuMNQwTO2_yAzksRQKT/4jn/dnlJmHP_SgSI5oHHoYTh7Q/h0/h001.naBdUhpeAeLfCoPVqvyi_yY-0VxzIbH4roYq8Fw_8QA)
* * *
**_Defying Trump’s Gerrymandering Powergrab_** When Texas Governor Greg Abbott called the state legislature back for a special session, it wasn’t to help families and communities recovering from devastating floods. It was to do Donald Trump’s bidding to gerrymander the state to deliver five extra Republican districts in Congress. The Democratic Caucus skipped town, leaving Republicans without a quorum to execute on Trump’s demands. As **WFP National Director Maurice Mitchell**[said in a national AP wire story](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoc5lroAYgnBM-pxs59wzI1RCr-sFsbJ27GvC1uuBbStoNGBqBh6Z4L71iFzR5U3Hy9qmrlB_Dnr5qoUaB4sY0kqC5Ub4nE2zfxzxgqtNOIKOJlyWlb7yWNggDLB1wFaMU9njBbd5ovmq6F4XYUqzNNNBdX9SUgQz_-piTx50O6rrHXtoWiJIY1zItT3qJ5H3j-wxGn0lOo0NYcSBTYybsQr2K__4jGDo2SU3FwCoIBl5F5_43bh-B_6CWII0y_aWa83qXskcdRu7PihQLIafbyTfb-B_qboUCkgRvJoPS5V2mil82ogZ3iREjMpDVS6mjwPwEab6D6gZG_l2Evxrv51Txt4MMO7Jqtt8zotu5fdJ/4jn/dnlJmHP_SgSI5oHHoYTh7Q/h1/h001.af63SX8vr3NjWNollp-st8_cq4VTjC4umaPi4WkgjWs), they were “taking real risks in protecting all of our rights” against “an authoritarian president who only understands the fight.” **Texas WFP** got to work with partners at Texas for All to turn out residents for local rallies, deliver testimony at regional hearings, and organize a national day of action to oppose Trump’s power grab, anchored by a 5,000-person strong rally in Austin. [](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9uM_K6dPs3zdscjDmx9hBCVavc6dSrXHGZsyQ9zvfKHSPY5Mc__aitGXzS_sRBlcadrwqMTkz1AK_xeBRG8HhV8gCvYMOVQQ04gFG8254MR6QbS3eJgnj2WZaSlPR4PnyaVNOy8H2vs2P9CM-lc5er0LweWbsGGifwhNABHXzXMAH2QIYHV44yuDFR-IAsEZjcHbhXwUBC98ytQOZ02i_TNy3NEVdU-CoY-XeFlGgIn9ociaPTMFfuWzoZ7p85djwb-RlAuHJgPbbwFNvIUD9qV0CkoB-FOKqyrdnfcHSI6GT65RfEpIn9Ut2oyEbu3fY/4jn/dnlJmHP_SgSI5oHHoYTh7Q/h2/h001.g1Xid7dfqCluGEnyVeto7WNY4l85qS9prvtgNRTsCSs) _More than 5K turned out for a rally in Austin to protest Trump’s power grab_ WFP members around the country turned out for solidarity rallies. **New York WFP** anchored a rally with lawmakers who announced a plan to fight back with New York’s line. And **California WFP** came out in support of Gov. Gavin Newsom's plan to redistrict the state to fight fire with fire and add Democratic-leaning districts and held a well-attended organizing call with WFP champs **US Rep. Lateefah Simon** and **Texas state Sen. Molly Cook**. [](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T9uM_K6dPs3zdscjDmx9hBCVavc6dSrXHGZsyQ9zvfKHSPY5Mc__aitGXzS_sRBlca16otm52sohiM-h7tud7Pq2T9gxhZh3z6m3uc5T_S9buNO08ELRxP4G0E9y30SbTA-x7-dl3fHxvwMnW5miqvBqCBxXxiCCcn8p5cpIonqVnRqJJrV2b-lpLBuq-FBXiORPFt0Hjf7fQYnOfodn3o6HsOro639iyjhI2ldACRtbbHNKbMpVaFF7uEgWVN3is6ftI9B2mxuel1Ii_7lyvccJHjex6zjs7nQtaVBq_Obz2R_khM7aUzIIf3T1NiiPqI/4jn/dnlJmHP_SgSI5oHHoYTh7Q/h3/h001.FkX_thsOwO82rHtEazVGF9blW8XW9tg1IZ_osOA1Qyk) _NY WFP Co-Director Jasmine Gripper leading a New York City rally in solidarity with the Texas lawmakers fleeing the Trump/Abbott gerrymandering push_
* * *
**_Major Endorsement Alert: Greg Casar_** While Texas may have passed their rigged Congressional maps in a desperate attempt to prevent the GOP from losing the House, we’re fighting back. One of the candidates most at risk was **Congressman Greg Casar** — and last month, we proudly endorsed him for re-election. A proud Texan and son of immigrants, Greg began his career as a labor organizer, fighting for living wages and dignity for working people. On the Austin City Council, he delivered major wins, from paid sick days to affordable housing. And for the past three years in Congress, Greg has worked hand-in-hand with WFP to continue these fights, making sure the needs of working people in Texas — and across the country — stay front and center. With his 2026 campaign for TX-37 officially underway, it’s time to show Greg that we’re still behind him. [**Split a donation between Greg’s campaign and WFP to help send him back to Congress in 2026, alongside a working families majority.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquqxZ_WMtWQ5nsYnjR236T98jiitdyMNqEGOX54ErvUQPVT6atjHI89u_KddltDOe2qe1C9yy_yFJvEkGkrBsqLDeEa_bkL8Z1zrlT4boqF5EZFRnqhSEUBoJ6fUgN-eNRDXZnsTLjoyYiatL5oKZ_dD6EFdc_vSrrPlTQRLA_UhkE7rBEdVJKh4PEKwTSUz9BfyJdeL95vHunIbNbF6uFReWxY5pqc1QE_ulyFDNF5bC7UQRdoedWGjm3Jmm40RumAicCHEKSuTJVWz4tIfhtWYCpHpCXn_W252Suhk2NNA-YRQNrcNiOW1F9VfALDVjrde4mXdTODIwrY7g8tzJhheGXznNXQqvXGCITqEF0FZg/4jn/dnlJmHP_SgSI5oHHoYTh7Q/h4/h001.khM-5SFLdK9NcJU_1nclDvo_6-IisfKWWNvLCZCtxe8)
* * *
**_Winning Critical Protections for Working Families in Delaware_** Recently, Delaware experienced the first property reassessment in 40 _years_ , resulting in shocking increases for many residents, and shifting the state’s tax burden onto homeowners rather than businesses. WFP legislators pushed for a full reassessment to fix the state’s upside-down tax system, a solution that would have addressed the root problem instead of offering temporary fixes. While that proposal wasn’t considered, WFP legislators didn’t back down. **Their persistence secured critical protections for working people, including flexible payment plans to prevent homeowners from losing their homes over unpaid taxes.** Thanks to their leadership, Delaware homeowners received a lifeline during the special session — but the underlying issue, the unfair tax system itself, still remains unaddressed. [**Read more about the special session in Delaware and what WFP electeds are doing to fight for relief for Delaware’s residents.** ](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMc_zy6EO38-dPqL8yd0UjKs7PLK9447PbBZ673gFgokOXIQFwGt3gnTmY2x2uOCUw1rU6RoQw_l1_hjukOopE4BYRSS80c29zVpG5jWFm1AyqKQbeyfssydcFTd8ePI5vqtAqOqS2FCpxWHj64_HJ3CFxD_eGAjQ02YBNeB_8y3O2xs5J10Q54iGffndF0VpBT6dYjY-4NclX01FwcAf8a-ZwyYeR4UvWOPN2hvnvx2Bzr1m8H4H4L0FDnzqMQtDTm6T6x6qlTLNBIYiGhJaEJO2wSe6hgLXVttuazc72azG_HC9wUJK12bf-EXgUXmQiScQaUkmFjsvyOEtNu1kf5ZrRrwW-6lgUAEfNdBbE6zeGwiazEqINbQe2Nv7MoWSNp50SkTH43HMihhgpbM0Zoo_KZ7_E5Yc_dF6n8FXi9szEA2p__0_KRNQu-vi8v45bNcY3Ac4ssiKVM-0hSEru48/4jn/dnlJmHP_SgSI5oHHoYTh7Q/h5/h001.sTBzIu7RfQzg-7Xafe7r5xU4ig-Pxz2ZrO6d0ZyF2p8)
* * *
**_Getting Into the Groove With WFP at Outside Lands_** As part of our mission to meet people where they are at, WFP posted up at the **2025 Outside Lands Music Festival** in San Francisco where we had a WFP’s People’s Parlor booth featuring a photobooth, free manicures from our nail techs, cute stick on freckles that sparkled, and swag for attendees who signed on to throw down with WFP. And our fave **Big Freedia** DJ’d sets and got real with WFP’s Nelini Stamp. clean_body: | | | Peter, We’ve got a LOT of exciting news to share from the past month, so we put together this WFP newsletter just for you! Keep reading to catch up on our recent wins and updates for the fight ahead. Notching More WFP Victories! If you thought this year’s Working Families Party wave was just in New York City – think again. Working Families Party candidates scored primary wins from Seattle to Detroit to Tucson this past month. Wins like these are only possible because of WFP members like you who donate their time, energy, and resources to electing champions for working people at every level of government, and taking the fight directly to the billionaires. Defying Trump’s Gerrymandering Powergrab When Texas Governor Greg Abbott called the state legislature back for a special session, it wasn’t to help families and communities recovering from devastating floods. It was to do Donald Trump’s bidding to gerrymander the state to deliver five extra Republican districts in Congress. The Democratic Caucus skipped town, leaving Republicans without a quorum to execute on Trump’s demands. As WFP National Director Maurice Mitchell, they were “taking real risks in protecting all of our rights” against “an authoritarian president who only understands the fight.” Texas WFP got to work with partners at Texas for All to turn out residents for local rallies, deliver testimony at regional hearings, and organize a national day of action to oppose Trump’s power grab, anchored by a 5,000-person strong rally in Austin. More than 5K turned out for a rally in Austin to protest Trump’s power grab WFP members around the country turned out for solidarity rallies. New York WFP anchored a rally with lawmakers who announced a plan to fight back with New York’s line. And California WFP came out in support of Gov. Gavin Newsom's plan to redistrict the state to fight fire with fire and add Democratic-leaning districts and held a well-attended organizing call with WFP champs US Rep. Lateefah Simon and Texas state Sen. Molly Cook. NY WFP Co-Director Jasmine Gripper leading a New York City rally in solidarity with the Texas lawmakers fleeing the Trump/Abbott gerrymandering push Major Endorsement Alert: Greg Casar While Texas may have passed their rigged Congressional maps in a desperate attempt to prevent the GOP from losing the House, we’re fighting back. One of the candidates most at risk was Congressman Greg Casar — and last month, we proudly endorsed him for re-election. A proud Texan and son of immigrants, Greg began his career as a labor organizer, fighting for living wages and dignity for working people. On the Austin City Council, he delivered major wins, from paid sick days to affordable housing. And for the past three years in Congress, Greg has worked hand-in-hand with WFP to continue these fights, making sure the needs of working people in Texas — and across the country — stay front and center. With his 2026 campaign for TX-37 officially underway, it’s time to show Greg that we’re still behind him. Winning Critical Protections for Working Families in Delaware Recently, Delaware experienced the first property reassessment in 40 years , resulting in shocking increases for many residents, and shifting the state’s tax burden onto homeowners rather than businesses. WFP legislators pushed for a full reassessment to fix the state’s upside-down tax system, a solution that would have addressed the root problem instead of offering temporary fixes. While that proposal wasn’t considered, WFP legislators didn’t back down. Their persistence secured critical protections for working people, including flexible payment plans to prevent homeowners from losing their homes over unpaid taxes. Thanks to their leadership, Delaware homeowners received a lifeline during the special session — but the underlying issue, the unfair tax system itself, still remains unaddressed. Getting Into the Groove With WFP at Outside Lands As part of our mission to meet people where they are at, WFP posted up at the 2025 Outside Lands Music Festival in San Francisco where we had a WFP’s People’s Parlor booth featuring a photobooth, free manicures from our nail techs, cute stick on freckles that sparkled, and swag for attendees who signed on to throw down with WFP. And our fave Big Freedia DJ’d sets and got real with WFP’s Nelini Stamp. Upcoming Events Joining the WFP Call Team is an opportunity to make a major impact in elections and policy fights across the country. We’ll keep you up to date on virtual phone banking opportunities that will allow you to directly reach voters, to share with them what we’re fighting for and how they can help. This month’s WFP National Welcome Gathering is Thursday, September 18 at 7PM ET. At the gathering, you can hear from WFP organizers who will share what we’re working on nationwide and any ways to get plugged in. If you’re feeling anxious about this political moment and the fight ahead, the Welcome Gathering is an opportunity to ground yourself in our shared values and community. We hope to see you there! Plug in with WFP in Georgia, Pennsylvania, Arizona, Connecticut, California, New York, New Jersey, Minnesota, Louisiana, Virginia, Maryland, and other states across the country and join our fight for working people. Thanks for catching up with us, Peter! As fall approaches, our movement enters a pivotal moment. Local general elections in November will shape communities nationwide, and every win will set the stage for the 2026 midterms. body:
Ballots for all!

|
## Write Yourself In
Wouldn't it be nice to win elected office without worrying about getting on the ballot first? How about if instead of campaigning for weeks and months, you just did it for one day? That's how dozens of write-in candidates win office every year. There are many many offices in PA with no candidates this year and it's not too late. With a little effort on election day, you could hold one of these offices. Here's how it works. **1\. Reach out to your local Division of Elections office and find out if any offices are open and pick one that's right for you.** **2\. Give them a list of alias someone might write in meaning to vote for you.** **3\. Print out some sort of handout with your name and the office you're running for. We'd love to help you out with this especially if you are willing to do this as a Forwardist and promote us at the same time.** **4\. On Election Day, you and any volunteers you recruit stand at polling places, distribute hand outs and explain why voters should write you in.** We spend a lot of time talking about ballot access and eligibility. This is a shortcut that can be perfect for political newcomers and can make voting feel local and alive. Let us know if you have any questions.

clean_body: Ballots for all! | Write Yourself In Wouldn't it be nice to win elected office without worrying about getting on the ballot first? How about if instead of campaigning for weeks and months, you just did it for one day? That's how dozens of write-in candidates win office every year. There are many many offices in PA with no candidates this year and it's not too late. With a little effort on election day, you could hold one of these offices. Here's how it works. 1\. Reach out to your local Division of Elections office and find out if any offices are open and pick one that's right for you. 2\. Give them a list of alias someone might write in meaning to vote for you. 3\. Print out some sort of handout with your name and the office you're running for. We'd love to help you out with this especially if you are willing to do this as a Forwardist and promote us at the same time. 4\. On Election Day, you and any volunteers you recruit stand at polling places, distribute hand outs and explain why voters should write you in. We spend a lot of time talking about ballot access and eligibility. This is a shortcut that can be perfect for political newcomers and can make voting feel local and alive. Let us know if you have any questions. PA Forward Party endorsements so far in 2025 \- Independent candidate for Derry Township School Board Director \- Democratic candidate for Bucks County Sheriff \- Republican candidate for Delaware County Controller \- Republican candidate for Lower Macungie Township Commissioner You can check out the pledge they signed . Join us September 15th at 8pm for our Monthly Statewide call. You'll have things you want to talk about, We willtoo! Click below to see more Isabelle Harman announced her campaign for congress Tuesday. She's been involved with the PA Forward Party for a long time and has built relationships with many among us. We wish her the best and suggest you keep your eye on this race. Help support these events from our partner organizations. And Join in a conversation with other PA Forward Supporters on Slack! Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.
Upcoming events
As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA016/1/99735/images/Pittsburgh%20School%20board%20forum%208.5x11.png]
Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students.
Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader.
With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color.

Your vote shapes our justice system!
Moderator: Rachel Bracken, Alliance for Justice (AFJ), Senior Regional State Courts Manager
Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. She also coordinated AFJ’s networks of law professors, attorneys, and political donors to advocate around federal judicial nominations and federal courts’ impact on our constitutional rights and freedoms.

This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .

Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.
