**THC regulations**

Among Abbott’s top priorities and one of the issues that triggered the special sessions was the the burgeoning unregulated hemp-derived THC market – which has thrived for years with no uniform testing requirements, no age limits on purchase, and no packaging or marketing restrictions.

Two items on his list addressed the issue. One was for lawmakers to craft a regulatory framework similar to that the state uses to regulate alcohol – with limits on who can sell, as well as when and where they can sell, age limits, packaging and testing requirements, open-container laws and more.

The other, apparently offered as an alternative, was a simple 21-and-up limit on who could buy and possess low-dose THC items.

Neither made it to his desk.

Our mission is simple — harness Austin’s cultural, professional and civic energy to build an elite baseball franchise. Our vision is a stadium district that serves as a “third downtown,” modeled on successful mixed-use projects in Atlanta and Arlington. Brandon Creighton’s switch from lawmaking to Texas Tech leader signals a new era for higher ed,” Texas Tribune's Jessica Priest \-- "As the clock wound down on the year’s , Lt. Gov.Dan Patrick , the powerful leader of the Texas Senate, took a few minutes to say goodbye to his right-hand man, Sen.Brandon Creighton : The architect of a recent bevy of laws reshaping higher education in Texas — from the ban on diversity, equity and inclusion programs to limits on protests and faculty’s influence on campuses — was stepping down to take a new job overseeing those very changes. Texas Tech regents voted Thursday to name the Conroe Republican their , the university system’s top job, betting that his political connections and influence at the Capitol will help secure funding, expand research opportunities and elevate the system’s profile. Chancellors are at the helm of each university system’s fleet of campuses, and Texas universities have increasingly turned to politicians to lead them, a shift that Patrick celebrated Wednesday. He pointed to the Texas A&M; and University of Texas systems’ new chancellors — Glenn Hegar , the state’s former state comptroller and a former state senator, and former state Rep. John Zerwas , respectively — as models of the kind of political leadership he believes universities need. ”There’s a whole new look at least in Texas of who [university leaders] think should lead universities, people with legislative experience, people who have been accountable to the people, people who have a record,” Patrick said. “You don’t just have to have nine letters behind your name and some education degree to run a university when it really takes more than just that.” Experts say regents have increasingly prioritized political savvy over academic leadership when picking university system leaders, a statewide and national shift they warn could make higher education less independent and give politicians greater influence over academics, research and campus life. Barrett Taylor , a higher education governance expert at the University of North Texas, said Creighton’s selection signals that Texas is entering a new phase in that transformation. “Enacting laws was part of the agenda for reshaping public higher education in Texas, but it’s not where it ends,” he said. “There are going to be additional steps, and this is probably one of those steps.” Renée Cross , senior executive director at the University of Houston’s Hobby School of Public Affairs, agreed. “It just makes too much sense for public universities — and for those in power — to have, for lack of a better word, their ‘lieutenants’ in these high-ranking positions,” she said. “If Lt. Gov. Patrick really wants to change the system of higher education in Texas — and he’s been pretty open about wanting to — of course you’d want people you know and trust running these large university systems. I don’t see that changing anytime soon. Even if Democrats controlled the state years from now, I could see them doing the same thing.” In an interview with The Texas Tribune, Texas Tech Board Chair Cody Campbell said regents believe the chancellor’s job is fundamentally different from a campus president’s, and should emphasize representation before state leaders rather than academic oversight. “We do not need a chancellor who knows how to run the math department,” he said." | PLEASE NOTE : You are receiving the PAID subscriber version of Must Read Texas — FOR TODAY ONLY — so you can see what you are missing. | | Become a PAID subscriber for $7/mo or $70/yr! | “Houston man charged with murder in shooting of 11-year-old boy after door knocking prank,” via AP \-- "Police have charged a Houston man with murder in who knocked on the door of a home and ran away as a prank, police said Tuesday. The 42-year-old man, identified by authorities as Gonzalo Leon Jr., was taken into custody and booked into the Harris County Jail in Houston early Tuesday. On local property records, Leon matches the name of the owner of the home where police say the boy knocked on the door. Court records did not list an attorney for Leon to comment on the allegations. The boy, Julian Guzman , and a cousin had been attending a birthday party Saturday night when they “became bored and wanted to ring doorbells, or play ‘ding dong ditch,’” according to a probable cause affidavit. The prank commonly called “ding dong ditching” involves ringing a doorbell or knocking on a door and fleeing before someone inside opens the door. Police departments around the country have issued public service announcements in recent months warning people that such actions aren’t funny but dangerous. Homeowners have no way of knowing it’s “just a prank,” according to a June by the Georgetown, Kentucky Police Department. Guzman’s cousin told investigators he and Guzman knocked several times on Leon’s door and ran away. Fellow Conservative,

You may not know me yet, but my name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m a lifelong Minnesotan, former Navy SEAL, and Marine Corps veteran running for U.S. Senate in 2026. I’m stepping into this fight because Minnesota—and our country—needs a new voice to stand up for our values, and I’m asking for your help to make it happen.

I grew up in Bloomington, Minnesota, playing hockey and learning teamwork from my working-class parents. _**On my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after 9/11, I enlisted in the Marine Corps to serve our nation.**_

**Over 21 years, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries as a Marine and Navy SEAL, putting my life on the line to defend our freedoms.** I earned my undergraduate degree from the University of Minnesota, a Master’s from Harvard, a Master’s Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. But at my core, I’m a regular guy who wants to make my mom proud and fight for the Minnesota I love.

Right now, Minnesota and America face a critical moment. The radical policies of Tim Walz and his lieutenant governor—who’s running to replace retiring Senator Tina Smith—threaten our way of life. From the unrest in Minneapolis in 2020 to attacks on our police, their agenda doesn’t reflect the Minnesota I know. _**This open Senate seat in 2026 is our chance to take back our state and stop the left’s push toward extremism. Just like in Georgia, where one seat flipped the Senate majority in 2021, Minnesota’s vote could decide the future of the U.S. Senate.

**_ **But here’s the challenge: I’m a new face, and the Democrats are already raising millions to keep this seat.** I’ve noticed you haven’t been active lately, Fellow Conservative, and I get it—the news can feel overwhelming, and it’s easy to think the fight’s already won. clean_body: Your past support has helped Republicans win tough battles, and we need you now to introduce me to Minnesota voters | Fellow Conservative, You may not know me yet, but my name is Adam Schwarze, and I’m a lifelong Minnesotan, former Navy SEAL, and Marine Corps veteran running for U.S. Senate in 2026. I’m stepping into this fight because Minnesota—and our country—needs a new voice to stand up for our values, and I’m asking for your help to make it happen. I grew up in Bloomington, Minnesota, playing hockey and learning teamwork from my working-class parents. On my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after 9/11, I enlisted in the Marine Corps to serve our nation. Over 21 years, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries as a Marine and Navy SEAL, putting my life on the line to defend our freedoms. I earned my undergraduate degree from the University of Minnesota, a Master’s from Harvard, a Master’s Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. But at my core, I’m a regular guy who wants to make my mom proud and fight for the Minnesota I love. Right now, Minnesota and America face a critical moment. The radical policies of Tim Walz and his lieutenant governor—who’s running to replace retiring Senator Tina Smith—threaten our way of life. From the unrest in Minneapolis in 2020 to attacks on our police, their agenda doesn’t reflect the Minnesota I know. This open Senate seat in 2026 is our chance to take back our state and stop the left’s push toward extremism. Just like in Georgia, where one seat flipped the Senate majority in 2021, Minnesota’s vote could decide the future of the U.S. Senate. But here’s the challenge: I’m a new face, and the Democrats are already raising millions to keep this seat. I’ve noticed you haven’t been active lately, Fellow Conservative, and I get it—the news can feel overwhelming, and it’s easy to think the fight’s already won. But it’s not. Right now, donations are slowing, and the other side is quietly building its war chest. I’m thinking of patriots like you who’ve supported conservatives before. Your past support has helped Republicans win tough battles, and we need you now to introduce me to Minnesota voters. It’s not about the amount—it’s a signal that you’re with me, that you believe Minnesota and America deserve a conservative fighter who’s served our nation and will serve you in Washington. As a Navy SEAL, I’ve thrived in the most challenging missions and am ready for this campaign. But I can’t do it without you. We need thousands of grassroots supporters, not Hollywood elites or mega-donors like the Democrats rely on. Minnesota hasn’t voted Republican for president since 1976, but this race is winnable. I’m running to secure our borders, support law enforcement, revive our economy, and protect our freedoms. Please, chip in $5 today to help me introduce myself to Minnesotans and fight for our shared values. With steadfast resolve, Adam Schwarze Retired Navy SEAL Republican Candidate for U.S. Senate - Minnesota Former Navy SEAL officer Marine Corps Veteran Proud Minnesotan FOLLOW ADAM ON SOCIAL MEDIA | | Paid for by Schwarze for Senate Adam Schwarze is a former Navy SEAL and Marine. More than a fifth of Americans get their health care coverage through Medicaid, Peter. About half of America’s children are covered by Medicaid or the Children’s Health Insurance Program.
Medicaid keeps our entire health care system functioning. Funding from Medicaid helps rural health centers stay open and keeps folks healthy so they don’t have to deal with growing long-term costs later on. It even helps boost states’ economies — like passing Medicaid Expansion did right here in NC.
But Republicans’ budget plan has slashed Medicaid funding, imperiling our health care system and putting folks’ health in jeopardy. They are playing politics with people’s LIVES, Peter.

#
---
Peter, We are nearing the end of the fiscal year, and Congress needs to pass a budget to keep the government open. We have a deep divide to cross in order to get there. There’s one person in D.C. you might not know: Russell Vought. Vought is the head of the Office of Management and Budget, or OMB. Like most other members of the Trump regime, Vought’s goals are to dismantle the federal government. Starting with the worldview of wanting to make the federal workforce feel “traumatized,” Vought is behind the ways in which the Trump administration is lawlessly and illegally taking apart the federal workforce and ignoring Congress’s authority and direction on how to spend federal dollars. Vought’s position also underscores one of the many lies Trump made on the campaign trail. **Walk away from Project 2025? Yeah right. Russell Vought is one of the authors.** What does all this mean for us? Democrats are working hard to make _certain_ that Trump and Vought have zero wiggle room on how to spend the tax dollars we have authorized. name: Saikat Chakrabarti
subject: YOU can get stock trading in Congress banned
body:
With new developments in Congress, we could actually get a ban passed on congressional stock trading!

| | | | | [|
---](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=6202a88dae&e=bf17056ae8)
| | | | | | Dear Friend,With new developments in Congress, we could actually get a ban passed on congressional stock trading!
---
| [Join a citizen lobbying team](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=f4a74c4f22&e=bf17056ae8)
---
| | A group of eight Democrats and eight Republicans just announced legislation in the House that would make it illegal for members of Congress to own or trade stocks. As I’m sure you know, congress people today often have access to confidential information about companies and markets, and [**many of them just happen to make the right stock trades at the right times to make millions of dollars**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=0beb32c749&e=bf17056ae8). Not only is this infuriating and corrupt, it can lead lawmakers to make decisions that good for their stock portfolios, but bad for the country.
---
[|
---](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=e78f61186f&e=bf17056ae8)
| | Even when they aren’t engaging in corrupt behavior, the mere perception that they are is a big reason why Congress has lost so much trust as an institution. A ban on congressional stock trading would do a lot to help restore some of that trust.The thing is, even though we have this bipartisan bill to ban stock trading, it won’t go anywhere unless it gets a floor vote. That’s why I was excited to see that Rep. Anna Paulina (a Republican) said she would file a discharge petition to force a vote on this bill if Speaker Mike Johnson doesn’t bring it up for a vote. This is exactly what I said Democrats should do [**in a video back in April**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=7f823d4f7a&e=bf17056ae8)**.** Discharge petitions can be very effective on bipartisan issues like this. But even with all this momentum, I don’t want to get everyone’s hopes up too much. This isn’t going to happen on its own, and you can bet that a lot of sitting congress members are going to do everything they can to figure out a way to weaken this bill or make it just disappear. We can’t let them! That’s why, for the past couple months, our campaign has been [**recruiting people across the country to create citizen lobbying**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=97ccde8010&e=bf17056ae8)**teams**. Congress constantly gets pressure from big corporations, big donors, and special interest groups lobbying them on specific bills. It’s much rarer for them to get calls from constituents lobbying for specific legislation. That’s why it’s an effective way to get legislation passed — especially if it’s bipartisan legislation like this where there is no excuse for it to get blocked! So if we can get a citizen lobbying group in every district lobbying their representative, we may actually be able to pass a ban on congressional stock trading. Maybe even this month![**Sign up to join one of these groups**](https://saikat.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6ed3ace2702e5b912b1693cee&id=4b1ad2bf95&e=bf17056ae8) and we’ll schedule a call very soon to start organizing. When you click, you’ll see instructions on what you can do to team up and go lobby your representative. How amazing would it be if we got SOMETHING good done in the midst of all that’s going bad? I really think we can.Best,Saikat
---
|
---

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

It’s been a little over 24 hours since we announced our second 2026
Democratic primary endorsement, and the momentum has been incredible!

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jd-em-20250905-2-at?refcode=em20250905-36993&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&refcode2=36993_1203867_2lNKsS&akid=36993%2E1203867%2E2lNKsS ]A post on X from Justice Democrats (@justicedems). The tweet reads:
'Justice Democrats is so proud to endorse our second primary challenger of
the cycle: @Angela4CA. Jimmy Gomez got to DC & closed the door behind him.
Angela is running to bring unbought leadership to #CA34 that will fight
back against Trump's fascism with the urgency it demands.'

If we’re going to defeat the establishment, AIPAC-backed Rep. Jimmy Gomez
in California’s 34th district and replace him with working-class champion
Angela Gonzales-Torres next year, it’s critical that we set Angela up for
success with a strong launch.

That’s why right now, every donation from Justice Democrats emails like
this one will go 100% to Angela’s campaign.

Because unlike Jimmy, Angela isn’t taking a dime of corporate PAC money.
Jimmy’s career in Washington is guided by accepting campaign checks in
exchange for his votes (like taking millions from AIPAC and refusing to
sign on to the ceasefire bill, or accepting contributions from crypto
lobbies and then voting to pass Trump’s corrupt crypto agenda), but Angela
is only guided by one thing: her community.

From her experience as the daughter of a deportee to her experience
working two jobs to put herself through community college, Angela is a
fighter, through and through — and she’s not afraid to go up against the
lobbies and super PACs who have bought Jimmy’s votes in Washington.

But that means [ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jd-em-20250905-2-at?refcode=em20250905-36993&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&refcode2=36993_1203867_2lNKsS&akid=36993%2E1203867%2E2lNKsS ]we need as many early, grassroots donations as possible
to take on Jimmy’s Super PAC-fueled war chest and WIN. Can you chip in
your first
contribution of $5 now?

[ https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jd-em-20250905-2-at?refcode=em20250905-36993&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&refcode2=36993_1203867_2lNKsS&akid=36993%2E1203867%2E2lNKsS ]Contribute $5

With your support, we can make Angela the next Justice Democrat in
Congress.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Contribute to Justice Democrats: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20250905-36993-footer&t=1002&refcode2=36993_1203867_2lNKsS&akid=36993%2E1203867%2E2lNKsS

## Army Football Safety Pulls Man from Burning Car
Army football player Larry Pickett Jr. and his father [pulled a man from a crashed vehicle](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OpDAUhE9jMiPjnwYCByutyHqT1WpD9LCfwT2PNjKebvn2I-YKk1ZJpfq-__f5DpHic_0DO9qwhrmEND_xfRKWgnleENx2Ro8OikPCJcdSO1FxlkIaLkYuzOwhUp11421AlKgatF1v-k7IQahms27Uzo9OqjH0CmAMvcFx8L0GGJTWuon2WhOjMFKIm5btYhYBRgnlwenOO6YF-lhSbh8pPsuGgWp6YW5d2huyWynHydQvJicmJ1jcRdCu6aqZnP79vdK8Vx5SKgsQ8YOgYuYEOVd-RPeBpfBH5h48Pz6JmJzOknJlaoqeqd-dNJ0xw9A12frjHYnieeuZFusOkb5vlB_7e1n5FQAA__-xIoTe) just before it exploded in flames early Sunday in Fort Montgomery, New York. The 20-year-old West Point cadet was heading home with his family when they came across a car crash surrounded by sparking power lines. Without hesitation, Larry and his dad sprinted to the burning vehicle and pulled the man from the driver's seat just moments before it was fully engulfed. [Watch a video here](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0Dtu6zAQheHVUJ2FEV-yChYXuBDSOE0QpCT4GFp0aNOQxha4-8DZQtpzgK_4v0725HLJt_O7u6JJ52QpVXvDfStIhKv16MKy5YjBUcCCfs3UBmhoOXB1gOkAykaXS7OyiyYhchQdmmFU4wD8CKJbjHJxnDioKIEPGmKSwmPUevATaHGUXTYvDSZQHEBL3nvlwSkBIroghxiYBIyZ6tpfar7Rgqm0-sS1D_XaFbMQ3Tcm_jE-Mz7v-963-qCHx9f_WhyFhYn5ycT_7_ts39rls35At5p433MpedMjk3C-ulx-Sfpzi6fhPwEAAP__ClBy7Q). name: Lindsey Graham
subject: The American Dream isn’t just a slogan.
body:
This is my story, but it’s not so different for many Americans. |
---
I want to share something from the heart with you, Fellow American.

**_My story._**
It isn't one of glitz and glamour -- it's about hard work, loss, and fighting for what's right. I'm reaching out to tell you why I'm in this fight for our future, and why I need you with me.

Neither of my parents finished high school. But they were hardworking and determined that their children would surpass their achievements.

Most of my growing up happened on the main street of a small textile mill town. My parents had a business establishment -- a combination beer joint, restaurant, liquor store, and pool hall -- known as the Sanitary Cafe right on Main Street in Central, SC. We all lived in the back of the bar where we worked late into the evening, especially my mom, before heading off to bed in the backroom.

[](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=aeb6d426853e44d487d92413ecf3802b&_e=LG7SjysxZR0LpWWIpGU5HXPMcs1R62EOKJF187AoHWtHt5AlDuo1WOwAx-EDG7Y6eZd9e3HPNCXKQzmY0JZC140esSKvP5EuTJpwa05lDR1Hq3vU8hJ1bqbfSHuntlDwsba6PdHAl9k0zcdmBE2MfexqzkvfbH7pbGTk3pPXEdBpqHDJSEIyJwqbJrSsboPm-IAFfb3fUZLGBjvXs_KMLbwdbESlD4HMw09uarWgifNnVKwoeRbcKZTCk63cUTHACaIRdvNRDO699_per1O7upaHvjm_Pd15f9Nt4lIIZQlHFyVXDbh2-4CFctByFwSt22xYEst9dq8H_1A0kLbUyPhtIGGQLHrCwkWdOwiiIVdoqOVRn1iM2wVTROwM-e3JsA7p8q3RqToRPrnyX_BwQDJG5XEsnsqhlUQwIk1KRzfXjuVILmVZzDssXCcvhbv6_z8rSSx96wTMioPrTG8oEhKGyoskF6P6SkAUKAzH5527rcCJ2fNmkTvyvsin3fNi9TDeuvssbiCBMNSa9fCj3rLG7mLNs-4gmiFwWqovk7l2NiwNn7etPrMAssN7oOIjEGGDb6-ajlZS4Xh_F11Fno7qyhSn7ZyTpfufCZLzqcrCkFTA13fboxJqROptvCdmN-B6lSPXGET3YlZoCb3SckUtMUriWAjuH81UoB0zZF17vKnwMHJSXuM-gUL5MuOi) I had no silver spoon in my mouth but I never felt I was missing out on something because I didn't live in a house like my friends did. I had a great life, and it was a great way to grow up.

I was the first in my family to attend college, but then life hit me hard. While I was in school, I lost my mom and dad within two years of each other. And just like that, I stepped up to help raise my 13-year-old sister, Darline, while coming back home on the weekends to help at our family business.

clean_body: This is my story, but it’s not so different for many Americans. | I want to share something from the heart with you, Fellow American. My story. It isn't one of glitz and glamour -- it's about hard work, loss, and fighting for what's right. I'm reaching out to tell you why I'm in this fight for our future, and why I need you with me. Neither of my parents finished high school. But they were hardworking and determined that their children would surpass their achievements. Most of my growing up happened on the main street of a small textile mill town. My parents had a business establishment -- a combination beer joint, restaurant, liquor store, and pool hall -- known as the Sanitary Cafe right on Main Street in Central, SC. We all lived in the back of the bar where we worked late into the evening, especially my mom, before heading off to bed in the backroom. I had no silver spoon in my mouth but I never felt I was missing out on something because I didn't live in a house like my friends did. I had a great life, and it was a great way to grow up. I was the first in my family to attend college, but then life hit me hard. While I was in school, I lost my mom and dad within two years of each other. And just like that, I stepped up to help raise my 13-year-old sister, Darline, while coming back home on the weekends to help at our family business. Fellow American, I learned some tough lessons early on. After law school, I joined the U.S. Air Force as a Judge Advocate General, serving as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after the people of South Carolina sent me to the United States Senate, I continued my service in the Air Force Reserves. I performed several short deployments in war zones like Afghanistan and Iraq, standing shoulder to shoulder with our brave men and women in uniform. My story isn't all that different from yours or most people across this great country. I didn't have anything handed to me. I worked hard, grew up quickly, and took on big responsibilities. But what shaped me most was listening to the hard -working South Carolinians who'd come by our family business, sharing their hopes and struggles, or hearing the perspectives of my brave colleagues in the military. Whether I agreed with them or not, those conversations built my understanding of what Americans need and deserve. Now, Fellow American, we all know our nation's in a tough spot -- we're divided, but there are some things we should agree on, plain and simple. 🇺🇸 We need a country where you can raise your family without fear, where the streets are safe. 🇺🇸 We need a country where the American Dream isn't just a slogan. It's alive, and every hard -working American has a real shot at it, no matter where they start. Sadly, there are folks in Washington, across the aisle, who don't see it that way. They're fine with open borders, allowing violent crime spill into our neighborhoods. They're okay with slapping higher taxes on hard-working folks like you, piling more burdens on your family. That isn't right, and I won't stand for it. So I'm coming to you with a simple ask, Fellow American. If you've got a few dollars to spare, | Fellow American, I know we can build a country that keeps our communities safe, rewards hard work, and gives every American a chance to chase their dreams -- just like I did. Thank you for taking a minute to hear my story. I'm grateful for you. Sincerely, Lindsey Graham In the United States Senate, South Carolina's Lindsey Graham has earned a reputation as a conservative, a problem-solver, and a leader who gets things done. He is a great friend to our men and women serving in uniform, a respected voice on national security matters, a leading advocate for cutting the out-of-control spending in Washington, and a champion for confirming conservative judges. | We want to make sure you're a proud member of Team Graham, and we don't want to bother you. Friend, You can't make this up. **While Trump claims he's fighting the fentanyl crisis, he pulled 60 DEA agents out of Arizona** to chase for political posturing in Washington, D.C. This is political theater at the expense of Arizona's safety. Our state Attorney General Kris Mayes put it perfectly:_"I find it absolutely outrageous that any president would endanger our entire country in this way." _ Now, she's demanding Trump return our agents immediately. **Here's what Trump's political stunt means for our state:**
* **60 DEA agents** have been pulled from the front lines of cartel activity
* **Arizona is left more vulnerable** to fentanyl trafficking
* **Our communities are less protected** while agents do photo ops in D.C.
* **Cartels are getting a free pass** while Trump plays politics.

Peter, I couldn't be more excited to share this news with you: **Today, I 'm proud to announce my campaign for re-election for Attorney General. **
I know I've got what it takes to give this campaign everything it needs to win. Why? Because I'm a mom, a former newspaper reporter, and one of the most popular elected officials in Arizona. And there's a simple reason for that: **I sue the sh*t out of Trump and anyone else who tries to hurt Arizona families.** Let me tell you how I got here. I used to be a Republican, thinking I was part of a party aligned with my values. But when I saw kids in cages at our border, when I watched Trump tear families apart, I knew I had to switch parties. And when January 6th happened, I knew I had to do something bigger.
So I left my job as a law professor at ASU, took a 50% pay cut, and ran for Attorney General in the toughest race of my life. We won by just 280 votes out of 2.5 million cast. Every single vote mattered.
And from day one, I've been fighting for a more just and more affordable Arizona. **Here's what I've been doing as your Attorney General: **
* I've filed 25 lawsuits against Trump and Musk, winning temporary restraining orders immediately in many of them.
* I'm Arizona's biggest water champion, suing the Saudis who are draining our aquifers to grow alfalfa they ship overseas.
* I'm taking on corporate landlords who collude to jack up rents.
* I work with local sheriffs and police chiefs to seize fentanyl from Mexico, and prosecute the cartels responsible for them.
* I successfully helped defeat the proposed Kroger-Albertsons merger that would have raised grocery prices.
* I go after elder abuse and utility companies that gouge customers.
* I'm fighting fraudsters and anyone trying to take advantage of everyday Arizonans.
* And I hold more press conferences and townhalls than any Democrat in Arizona, because transparency matters.

**But here's the thing: at least one of my GOP opponents can write seven-figure checks to fund his campaign.** Well, I certainly can't do that.

clean_body: | | Peter, I couldn't be more excited to share this news with you: Today, I 'm proud to announce my campaign for re-election for Attorney General. I know I've got what it takes to give this campaign everything it needs to win. Why? Because I'm a mom, a former newspaper reporter, and one of the most popular elected officials in Arizona. And there's a simple reason for that: I sue the sht out of Trump and anyone else who tries to hurt Arizona families. Let me tell you how I got here. I used to be a Republican, thinking I was part of a party aligned with my values. But when I saw kids in cages at our border, when I watched Trump tear families apart, I knew I had to switch parties. And when January 6th happened, I knew I had to do something bigger. So I left my job as a law professor at ASU, took a 50% pay cut, and ran for Attorney General in the toughest race of my life. We won by just 280 votes out of 2.5 million cast. Every single vote mattered. And from day one, I've been fighting for a more just and more affordable Arizona. Here's what I've been doing as your Attorney General: I've filed 25 lawsuits against Trump and Musk, winning temporary restraining orders immediately in many of them. I'm Arizona's biggest water champion, suing the Saudis who are draining our aquifers to grow alfalfa they ship overseas. I'm taking on corporate landlords who collude to jack up rents. I work with local sheriffs and police chiefs to seize fentanyl from Mexico, and prosecute the cartels responsible for them. I successfully helped defeat the proposed Kroger-Albertsons merger that would have raised grocery prices. I go after elder abuse and utility companies that gouge customers. I'm fighting fraudsters and anyone trying to take advantage of everyday Arizonans. And I hold more press conferences and townhalls than any Democrat in Arizona, because transparency matters. But here's the thing: at least one of my GOP opponents can write seven-figure checks to fund his campaign.** Well, I certainly can't do that. ~~ | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will be processed immediately and split between Kris Mayes and Jonathan Nez. | | | | | | We won together the first time. committee charged with doing oversight of DHS—all for doing oversight of
DHS. But this is about more than me. It is about how far the Republican

cruel agenda.

_All Democrats Sign On to Force Vote on Epstein Files. Not a Single Indiana Republican Has Done So_
__ Hoosiers and all Americans have been waiting for the release of the Epstein Files, as promised throughout the 2024 campaign. However, President Trump has ignored his promises and continues to hide information from the public that even the victims want released. Reps. Ro Khanna and Thomas Massie have led a bipartisan charge to get these files released. All 212 House Democrats, including Reps. Mrvan and Carson in Indiana, have signed on to force a vote on their release. However, just four Republicans have joined them, meaning the petition still needs two more signatures to force a vote. Not a single Republican in Indiana’s delegation has signed on to the discharge petition. It’s time for them to put the people first and let the American people see the files. ****_Mike Braun’s Changes to Utility Regulatory Structure are Too Little, Too Late for Hoosiers_
Governor Mike Braun appointed a new commissioner this week to the Office of Utility Consumer Counselor, and wants them to look into lower rates for Hoosiers. However, this is simply too little, too late for Hoosier families and ratepayers. Braun took no action as almost every utility company in the state asked for a rate increase over the past year. These rate increases have caused the average Hoosier household to see their utility bills rise by almost 20% in the past year. It’s time Hoosiers had a state government that truly stands up for them, and pays more than lip service on bringing down costs. ****_Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. body:
A few years ago, while visiting Shenandoah National Park, I took a bit of a tumble.
# [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/133?t=1&akid=4243%2E400544%2E5_aRZO)
A few years ago while visiting Shenandoah National Park, I took a _bit_ of a tumble.
I was hiking up the side of a mountain when I slipped on a loose rock. It was a total freak accident — I couldn’t believe it! But there I was, covered in dirt with a pain in my leg and ankle and three options:
* Get airlifted down in a helicopter,
* take eight National Park staff away from their jobs to carry me down,
* or hike down myself.

**I chose to walk back down the mountain** because I couldn’t stomach the idea of taking our National Park staff away from their work, even for a few hours. It turns out I hiked down all that way with a broken leg. I’ll be honest, I didn’t think my leg was actually broken at the time.
The federal workers who care for our public lands have absolutely crucial jobs to do. They preserve and protect our public lands for millions of visitors each year and for future generations. **Donald Trump has made it clear he intends to auction off our lands to extractive industries like Big Oil. He attempted to fire our dedicated National Parks and National Forests workers en masse.**
As Governor of New Mexico, I will be a fierce defender of our rivers, mesas, farmlands, and forests. I was hiking up the side of a mountain when I slipped on a loose rock. It was a total freak accident — I couldn’t believe it! But there I was, covered in dirt with a pain in my leg and ankle and three options: Get airlifted down in a helicopter, take eight National Park staff away from their jobs to carry me down, or hike down myself. I chose to walk back down the mountain because I couldn’t stomach the idea of taking our National Park staff away from their work, even for a few hours. It turns out I hiked down all that way with a broken leg. I’ll be honest, I didn’t think my leg was actually broken at the time. The federal workers who care for our public lands have absolutely crucial jobs to do. They preserve and protect our public lands for millions of visitors each year and for future generations. Donald Trump has made it clear he intends to auction off our lands to extractive industries like Big Oil. He attempted to fire our dedicated National Parks and National Forests workers en masse. As Governor of New Mexico, I will be a fierce defender of our rivers, mesas, farmlands, and forests. I will always stand up for the dedicated workers who serve our communities. As a former Secretary of the Interior, it breaks my heart to see what this administration is doing to exploit our lands and those who care for them. But just like the day I chose to hike down the mountain on my broken leg, I am determined to stand up and do right by the workers who proudly serve our nation. Be fierce, Deb P.S. **PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey folks!
💸 Day 3 of the **Durango 9R Dirty Dozen** : Durango 9R blew $209,000 of YOUR tax dollars on DEI “experts”—one day cost $69K. Parents want answers: why fund woke ideology over textbooks & teacher training?
Watch & share ➡️ **[Instagram](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) | [Facebook](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) | [X](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) | [TikTok](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
🎙️ Check out today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)! Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Colorado is juggling economic strain and shifting policies. Denver’s food scene saw [major turnover in August](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while wildfire-hit farmers can [now apply for USDA aid](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Section 8 vouchers are [covering rents near $3,900](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), fueling criticism of waste as a new report shows [60% of residents can’t afford the average home](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Polis ordered pharmacies to [keep giving COVID boosters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) without a doctor’s note, and in education, 55% of districts earned accredited ratings, though many [remain on the accountability clock](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** Trump is demanding Pfizer release its [COVID vaccine data](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), saying he’s seen “extraordinary” results privately but questioning why they remain hidden. Speaking of vaccines, Colorado’s health department is proposing to drop CDC guidance in favor of the American Academy of Pediatrics’ vaccine schedule—part of a push to [raise kindergarten MMR rates from 88% to 95% by 2027](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—sparking parental concern that exemptions could narrow and school requirements tighten.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** Sheriff Darren Weekly [defied the Freedom From Religion Foundation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) by reading at a Grandparents4Kids story hour, drawing praise for defending faith and family values. Dr. Brian Joondeph argues [transgenderism is “magical thinking”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) with tragic consequences, while critics blast Colorado’s unelected energy board for [giving Xcel control over appliances](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). C. J. Garbo cautions conservatives against [stripping gun rights by group identity](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), and Russ Minary calls for [cutting government “middlemen”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) to restore efficiency and lower costs.
This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, September 5, 2025.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[From ACIP to AAP: CDPHE proposes school vaccine rule shift amid 95% MMR goal](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Colorado’s health department is pushing new changes to school vaccine rules, and parents have less than two weeks to weigh in. CDPHE will appear before the State Board of Health on Oct. 15 to request a rulemaking hearing. Public comments are open now until 5 p.m. Friday, Sept. 19.
Parents on social media worry the changes could narrow exemptions or tighten school requirements. CDPHE says the edits are mostly technical, but its broader campaign to raise vaccination rates shows how high the stakes are.
CDPHE has made measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) rates among kindergarteners one of its “Wildly Important Goals.” The department wants to raise coverage from 88.3 percent in 2024 to 95 percent by 2027, the level it says is needed for herd immunity against measles.
For the fourth year in a row, MMR coverage among Colorado kindergarteners has stayed below 90 percent, holding steady at 88.03 percent. CDPHE warns that this plateau comes just as measles resurges globally. The U.S. has reported 1,088 cases across 33 jurisdictions as of May 29, 2025 with 96 percent unvaccinated.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado’s unelected energy board moves to give Xcel control over your appliances](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****
** BY CORY GAINES, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Starting in July 2026, Colorado’s new model energy code—mandated by HB22-1362—will require municipalities updating building codes to adopt stricter standards aimed at efficiency and emissions reduction.
* Larger homes must reach net-zero energy use, while mixed-fuel homes can keep gas appliances only if they meet tougher requirements than all-electric ones.
* The code mandates appliances be “demand response capable,” allowing utilities like Xcel to remotely reduce usage during peak demand, raising concerns over unelected boards granting corporations control inside homes.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

**[Reduce Taxes BY Eliminating the Government Middleman](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY ROSS MINARY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Russ Minary argues that unlike efficient free-market companies like Amazon and Costco, government is bloated, unaccountable, and constantly adds costly bureaucratic “middlemen”.
* He says taxpayers are forced to fund programs they may not want or use, from public schools to endless regulations, with no option to opt out like in the private sector.
* Calling taxes the “food of government,” Minary urges putting government on a “crash diet,” shifting services to the private market, and cutting unnecessary agencies to reduce the burden on Americans.

These claims, unverified as of now, have sparked sharp reactions on both sides of the aisle._
__
**[Douglas County sheriff defies Freedom From Religion Foundation after it targeted Grandparents4Kids story hour](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY STEVE MCKENNA | COMMENTARY | SEPTEMBER 4** _A funny thing happened on my way to my 60s. Concepts of tolerance my parents, teachers, and others taught me as a child evolved. In the 1960s, tolerance meant accepting others, not persecuting them because they were different from you or your friends. Now, in my 60s, it seems more about persecuting those who fail to tolerate to the satisfaction of a bullying minority of ideologues._
__

**[HGTV Can’t Save Small Town America. Fort Morgan Proves it.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | SEPTEMBER 3** _When HGTV came to Fort Morgan in 2023, we were promised a makeover, a shot at national attention, fresh energy, and maybe even prosperity. name: Sarah McBride
subject: I see it up close
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
It’s sad.
#
I want to share something with you as a person who sees it up close:
One of the most jarring things I’ve learned since coming to Congress is that for so many of my colleagues on the other side of the aisle, _**the cruelty really is the point**_.
In many cases, they believe the harm they’re inflicting — whether it’s gutting Medicaid and SNAP or targeting vulnerable communities — is aimed at people who don’t vote for them. But the truth is, they’re hurting their own constituents, _and they don’t seem to care._
What makes it worse is how much of it is for show.
Behind closed doors, they act one way — and they go out, put on this MAGA character to suck up to daddy and get clicks and attention on social media.
**It’s sad.**
Because Congress is a place of such profound importance, and there’s a profound potential to do good. It’s why I came here — to govern, lead with compassion, and fight for my neighbors in Delaware. To roll up my sleeves and stay focused on making life easier for working people, even when the other side treats cruelty as a strategy and public office as a show.
**If you believe that matters — if you want to keep this kind of leadership in Congress — I’m asking for your support today.** [**Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mcb-em-20250905-1?refcode=em20250905-2319&amount=5&refcode2=2319_21716_TB9Tlq&akid=2319%2E21716%2ETB9Tlq)

Thank you for being in this with me.
— Sarah

name: Wes Moore
subject: A note from me about Republican gerrymandering in Texas:
body:
Trump is putting his finger on the scale.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=558%2E1086043%2EoNj6ut)
Peter,
When I joined the Army, I swore an oath to support and defend the Constitution of the United States.
And the Constitution states that voters should pick their Members of Congress – _not the other way around._
But last week in Texas, Republicans gerrymandered the maps to all but guarantee they’ll pick up five U.S. House seats in the next election. **And they did it because the President of the United States asked them to do it.**
This undemocratic power grab isn’t any different from when Donald Trump asked Georgia election officials to “find him more votes” after he lost the 2020 election. Except now, he’s asking Republican governors across the country to find him more House seats so he can hold onto power in next year’s elections.
Trump is putting his finger on the scale to manipulate our fair and free elections because he knows his policies can’t win at the ballot box. He’s seen the power this team has to organize around a common purpose – and he’s afraid of what will happen when we come together to demand justice, fairness, and opportunity for all.
**When it comes to responding to this affront to our democracy, Peter, I believe we must keep all our options on the table.** We need to be able to have fair maps here in Maryland and across the country. Most of all, we must never turn our backs on the sacred promises guaranteed to every American by our Constitution.
**[If you’ve got my back in this fight to defend our free and fair elections, I’m asking you for your support. Please pitch in $5 or anything you can today to support my campaign.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-20250905-2?refcode=em-20250905-2&refcode2=558_1086043_oNj6ut&akid=558%2E1086043%2EoNj6ut)**

And they did it because the President of the United States asked them to do it. This undemocratic power grab isn’t any different from when Donald Trump asked Georgia election officials to “find him more votes” after he lost the 2020 election. Except now, he’s asking Republican governors across the country to find him more House seats so he can hold onto power in next year’s elections. Trump is putting his finger on the scale to manipulate our fair and free elections because he knows his policies can’t win at the ballot box. He’s seen the power this team has to organize around a common purpose – and he’s afraid of what will happen when we come together to demand justice, fairness, and opportunity for all. When it comes to responding to this affront to our democracy, Peter, I believe we must keep all our options on the table. We need to be able to have fair maps here in Maryland and across the country. Most of all, we must never turn our backs on the sacred promises guaranteed to every American by our Constitution. Elevate, Wes Moore

subject: Did anyone really think the sexual predator president who used to party with Jeffrey Epstein was going to release the Epstein files?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate
body:
Peter, it’s Jon. Before you log off for the weekend, I wanted to make sure you saw my note from yesterday.
Thanks in advance for reading.
\- Jon
_\---------- Begin forwarded message ---------
From: Jon Ossoff
Subject: re: Epstein Files
To: dpwillis67@gmail.com_
[](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-sep25.SYBMcx&refcode=em250905-1-f&t=1&akid=728%2E5691347%2EJ8ZTvF)

Remember when Donald Trump promised to release the Epstein files?
_Did anyone really think the sexual predator president who used to party with Jeffrey Epstein was going to release the Epstein files?_
Instead, he’s been busy taking away your health care to cut taxes for the rich and threatening to strip Americans of their citizenship and send them to foreign prisons.
We were told Donald Trump’s new GOP cared about working people.
But you can’t claim to be for working men and women when you defund their hospitals and nursing homes.
You can’t claim to be for working men and women when you defund school lunch programs that help feed little boys and girls whose hard-working parents are struggling to fill the fridge.
Let me tell you what it’s been like in Washington these last seven months.
The leaders of Georgia’s clinics and hospitals and nursing homes, caregivers for seniors and the disabled, nurses, teachers, food pantry directors — they all came to us and pleaded with Georgia's representatives in Congress: don’t do this. Don’t devastate health care. Don’t abandon seniors. Don’t starve kids.
Sen. Warnock and I listened. We fought that bill, and we voted No.
We put Georgia first.
But every Republican member of Congress who is supposed to represent Georgia put loyalty to Trump over loyalty to our state.
***
That brings me to the 2026 election.
_2026 is our only hope to recover Congressional power and reverse this descent toward one-man rule._
And here in Georgia I am the only Democratic U.S. Senator nationwide up for reelection in a state Trump won.
I am therefore MAGA’s #1 target for defeat.
_There is no path back without defending this seat — the seat that secured the Democratic majority four years ago._
This is a moment of struggle for the very substance of our Republic. This descent into one-man rule must be stopped.
**[If you share my outrage at this unprecedented corruption and abuse of power — and if you are determined to WIN — please chip in to my campaign today. This is the most important Senate race in the country, and I can’t win without you.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-sep25.SYBMcx&refcode=em250905-1-f&t=2&akid=728%2E5691347%2EJ8ZTvF)
**[DONATE](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-sep25.SYBMcx&refcode=em250905-1-f&t=3&akid=728%2E5691347%2EJ8ZTvF)**
Five years ago, here in Georgia, we lit a beacon of hope and possibility for the whole nation. It’s still shining.
And come next November, we will raise it higher.
In a landslide, we will do our part to end this spiral into chaos and corruption.
Thank you for your support.
\- Jon

I’d like to share it with you.
| Friend,
---
One of the things I love most about President Trump is that he always makes sure to show his appreciation and gratitude for those who fight alongside him.
---
**For example, he took the time to post my recent statement and thank me for everything I did to stop Tish James’ sham LAWFARE against him!**

The President’s support and friendship mean the world to me. But really, after all that he’s done for our country, I should be the one thanking _him_.

It would have been so easy for President Trump to give up and retire from politics after the disgraceful 2020 election.
---

Hey Derek,

It's that time of year. 🤓 You might be out getting last-minute supplies or packing lunches. While you're doing that, I’m heading back into the Capitol, packing a fight – for our kids.

[**You can help start this new year and new Senate session off strong by taking my short Back-to-School Survey before our midnight deadline.**](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/51632?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&code=jtk223-su-fl&t=1&akid=10292%2E434096%2EGyKMzN)
I'm getting back to the Senate to build on what we've done so far:
✅ **Introduced the School Lunch Debt Cancellation Act** – directing USDA to pay off ALL outstanding student meal debt
✅ **Led a bipartisan bill for more flexible milk options in school lunches** – because almost half of school kids that rely on school lunch programs are lactose intolerant
**✅ Forced Trump to release $7 BILLION in education funding** – that he’d _illegally_ frozen
Meanwhile, here’s what Trump's been up to:
🚨 **Mass layoffs at the Dept. of Ed** – threatening special education, financial aid, and civil rights enforcement
🚨 **Targeting trans kids & kids of color **– directing his civil rights team to investigate them for “unfair advantages”
🚨**Rolling back LGBTQIA+ protections** – allowing school meal programs to discriminate against queer kids
🚨 **Deep cuts to SNAP and Medicaid** – taking food and health care from children who need it
While I’m working for kids in PA + across the country, Trump is playing games with our kids’ futures. This is serious.
I need to hear from you. What’s worrying you? What’s falling through the cracks? How can we keep working together to fight for our kids?
**Please Derek, take a minute to fill out my short Back-to-School Survey.** ⬇️

We recently played a game with Judge Chris Taylor called Overruled/Sustained.

For example, one of these claims was “Cheese curds are superior to tater tots.” That one was sustained by the judge.
Here’s a big one: **“Judicial races don’t matter as much as other statewide races.”**

She believes it’s more crucial than ever to have trusted, impartial judges serving on the Wisconsin Supreme Court.
We’ve seen the damage that can be dealt by extreme judges on the bench, and that’s why we’re fighting to elect Judge Chris Taylor.

subject: Discriminatory Minneapolis Teachers’ Contract Update
body:
Investigation of International Terrorist Takedown

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH URGES FEDERAL PROBE OF RACIALLY DISCRIMINATORY
TEACHERS’ CONTRACT

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=36028&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj0tLThwaGZqSHB5RSZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=c298ad3d143b843bcc11e6032fcd7c5b68af42f12f4e60ee94e75302b4d20ce5]

We have formally requested
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=36006&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21pbm5lYXBvbGlzLXNjaG9vbHMtZXF1YWwtcHJvdGVjdGlvbi1jbGF1c2UtbGV0dGVycy0yMDI1Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=bdfbfaaccd08460796a4c65bb8a6240996030c00f8eb95520cce9c3d5b724a38]
that the Civil Rights Divisions of the U.S. Departments of Education
and Labor investigate the collective bargaining agreement between
Minneapolis Public Schools and the Minneapolis Federation of Teachers,
citing violations of the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth
Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.

In August 2022, we filed a lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=27927&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvbGF3c3VpdC1vdmVyLWRpc2NyaW1pbmF0b3J5LWNvbnRyYWN0Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=7998243dccd7e003c9e52dc55476e7ac7632f3a66eafa562b8ea40dcb08e875f]
on behalf of a Minneapolis taxpayer over a teachers’ contract that
provided discriminatory job protections to certain racial minorities.
The lawsuit was filed against the superintendent of the Minneapolis
Public Schools, the Minneapolis Public Schools, and the Minneapolis
Board of Education for violating the Equal Protection Guarantee of the
Minnesota Constitution.

In January 2025, the Minnesota Supreme Court issued an opinion
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=34235&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZGlzY3JpbWluYXRvcnktdGVhY2hlcnMtY29udHJhY3QvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=fa0889910a3ebc0c01e127b1311d6e0557cb5fdc1eae314a18f7475937626d79],
rejecting our lawsuit without addressing the constitutionality of the
contract.

In our letters
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=36006&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL21pbm5lYXBvbGlzLXNjaG9vbHMtZXF1YWwtcHJvdGVjdGlvbi1jbGF1c2UtbGV0dGVycy0yMDI1Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=bdfbfaaccd08460796a4c65bb8a6240996030c00f8eb95520cce9c3d5b724a38]
to the Civil Rights Divisions of the Departments of Education and
Labor, Judicial Watch urges the agencies to “open a formal
investigation” of Minneapolis public schools for civil rights
violations:

> Judicial Watch requests the Office for Civil Rights investigate
> Article 15 of the collective bargaining agreement between the
> Minneapolis Public Schools, Special District No. 1 (“MPS”) and
> the Minneapolis Federation of Teachers Local 59. The contract
> violates the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to
> the U.S. Constitution.

> Article 15 exempts teachers of color from MPS’s seniority-based
> layoffs and reassignments, which means, when layoffs or
> reassignments occur, the next senior teacher who is not “of
> color” would be laid off or reassigned. The contract also mandates
> that MPS reinstate teachers of color over more senior teachers who
> are not “of color.” Prior to the contract, teachers were laid
> off or reassigned in order of seniority, with the least senior
> teachers laid off or reassigned first, without regard to race or
> ethnicity. Similarly, teachers were reinstated in order of
> seniority, with the more senior teachers reinstated first, without
> regard to race or ethnicity. Article 15 has been effective as of
> July 1, 2021, and continues to be in effect today. In addition, MPS
> is currently negotiating with the teachers’ union concerning a new
> contract. There is no indication that this provision will not be
> included in the new contract.

***

> MPS’s Article 15 is repugnant to the U.S. Constitution’s
> guarantee of equal protection under the 14th Amendment. It is not
> only a discriminatory contract that threatens teachers’ jobs, but
> a blatant civil rights violation and cannot stand.

The letters conclude: “Should any portion of this complaint fall
outside the OCR’s [Office of Civil Rights] subject matter
jurisdiction, we request that you refer that portion to the Attorney
General for further action.”

Minneapolis Public Schools clearly discriminate against teachers based
on their race, and the school district is using taxpayer dollars to do
so. Let’s hope that the Departments of Education and Labor do a
better job of upholding civil rights law than the Minnesota Supreme
Court.

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FBI FOR RECORDS ON DEATH OF TERRORIST ‘MARWAN’

We’re looking to shed light on a law enforcement action that took
down a “Most Wanted” international terrorist.

We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=36022&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLW1hcndhbi1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDE5OTEvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=a698fa11a4d98edaa92bb9b70c751066a98ca745dace4f4ea2f1ef53580749d1]
against the U.S. Department of Justice for records related to the
killing of Malaysian-born terrorist Zulkifli bin Hir, also known as
“Marwan,” during a police raid (_Judicial Watch, Inc. v. U.S.
Department of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=36022&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLW1hcndhbi1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDE5OTEvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=a698fa11a4d98edaa92bb9b70c751066a98ca745dace4f4ea2f1ef53580749d1]
(No. 1:25-cv-01991)).

Zulkifli bin Hir aka “Marwan” was indicted
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=36023&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVzdGljZS5nb3YvYXJjaGl2ZS9vcGEvcHIvMjAwNy9BdWd1c3QvMDdfbnNkXzU3OC5odG1sP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=d1de746df04f257ee5e1cc2adc74b7cdc5fce7fbdc93df542395039247f63aaa]
by the Justice Department in August 2007 for conspiracy and providing
material support to terrorists:

> Zulkifli Abdhir, aka “Zulkifli Bin Abdul Hir, aka “Hulagu,”
> aka “Marwan,” age 41, a fugitive believed to be in the
> Philippines, is charged in the indictment with conspiracy to provide
> material support to terrorists and providing material support to
> terrorists. In September 2003, the U.S. government designated Abdhir
> as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist pursuant to Executive
> Order 13224. In March 2007, the State Department added him to the
> most-wanted list of its Rewards for Justice program and authorized a
> reward of up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest or
> conviction ...

In January 2015, Zulkifli bin Hir reportedly was killed
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=36024&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25uLmNvbS8yMDE1LzA0LzAzL3dvcmxkL3BoaWxpcHBpbmVzLW1hcndhbi1jb25maXJtZWQtZGVhZC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=b3c1fc6f70c2854522f435c31ff57a8a401db98d49cd29f9ad1e7c40c670ccf6]
during a raid by the Philippine National Police Special Action Force.
Forty-four members of the police’s elite force also died in the
assault.

A finger taken from a man killed in the raid was delivered to the FBI
for DNA analysis. The FBI stated
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=76435&L=36025&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25uLmNvbS8yMDE1LzA0LzAzL3dvcmxkL3BoaWxpcHBpbmVzLW1hcndhbi1jb25maXJtZWQtZGVhZF06P3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=051907e6a8cfedf64822748019985c21cad4a826c040dbe75c77ac46ca118226
“After a thorough review of forensic data and information obtained
from our Philippine law enforcement partners, the FBI has assessed
that terrorism subject, Zulkifli Abdhir ... is deceased and has been
removed from the FBI’s list of Most Wanted Terrorists.”

We sued after the FBI failed to respond to an April 25, 2025, FOIA
request for records on Zulkifli bin Hir (aka “Marwan”) and his
death during Oplan (Operation Plan) Exodus on January 25, 2015, in
Mamasapano, Maguindanao, Philippines. The request asked for records
about the collection, analysis, and chain of custody of a severed left
index finger alleged to belong to Marwan, as well as photographs of
his body and any related identification or forensic documentation.

Marwan was a high-profile international terrorist on the FBI’s Most
Wanted list with a $5 million reward. The operation that brought him
down over a decade ago was a major event in Philippine and U.S.
counterterrorism history. It’s time for transparency.

clean_body: Investigation of International Terrorist Takedown [INSIDE JW] JUDICIAL WATCH URGES FEDERAL PROBE OF RACIALLY DISCRIMINATORY TEACHERS’ CONTRACT [] We have formally requested [] that the Civil Rights Divisions of the U.S. Departments of Education and Labor investigate the collective bargaining agreement between Minneapolis Public Schools and the Minneapolis Federation of Teachers, citing violations of the Equal Protection Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. In August 2022, we filed a lawsuit [] on behalf of a Minneapolis taxpayer over a teachers’ contract that provided discriminatory job protections to certain racial minorities. The lawsuit was filed against the superintendent of the Minneapolis Public Schools, the Minneapolis Public Schools, and the Minneapolis Board of Education for violating the Equal Protection Guarantee of the Minnesota Constitution. In January 2025, the Minnesota Supreme Court issued an opinion [], rejecting our lawsuit without addressing the constitutionality of the contract. In our letters [] to the Civil Rights Divisions of the Departments of Education and Labor, Judicial Watch urges the agencies to “open a formal investigation” of Minneapolis public schools for civil rights violations: Judicial Watch requests the Office for Civil Rights investigate Article 15 of the collective bargaining agreement between the Minneapolis Public Schools, Special District No. 1 (“MPS”) and the Minneapolis Federation of Teachers Local 59. The contract violates the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. Article 15 exempts teachers of color from MPS’s seniority-based layoffs and reassignments, which means, when layoffs or reassignments occur, the next senior teacher who is not “of color” would be laid off or reassigned. The contract also mandates that MPS reinstate teachers of color over more senior teachers who are not “of color.” Prior to the contract, teachers were laid off or reassigned in order of seniority, with the least senior teachers laid off or reassigned first, without regard to race or ethnicity. Similarly, teachers were reinstated in order of seniority, with the more senior teachers reinstated first, without regard to race or ethnicity. Article 15 has been effective as of July 1, 2021, and continues to be in effect today. In addition, MPS is currently negotiating with the teachers’ union concerning a new contract. There is no indication that this provision will not be included in the new contract. * MPS’s Article 15 is repugnant to the U.S. Constitution’s guarantee of equal protection under the 14th Amendment. It is not only a discriminatory contract that threatens teachers’ jobs, but a blatant civil rights violation and cannot stand. The letters conclude: “Should any portion of this complaint fall outside the OCR’s [Office of Civil Rights] subject matter jurisdiction, we request that you refer that portion to the Attorney General for further action.” Minneapolis Public Schools clearly discriminate against teachers based on their race, and the school district is using taxpayer dollars to do so. Let’s hope that the Departments of Education and Labor do a better job of upholding civil rights law than the Minnesota Supreme Court. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FBI FOR RECORDS ON DEATH OF TERRORIST ‘MARWAN’ We’re looking to shed light on a law enforcement action that took down a “Most Wanted” international terrorist. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the U.S. Department of Justice for records related to the killing of Malaysian-born terrorist Zulkifli bin Hir, also known as “Marwan,” during a police raid (Judicial Watch, Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice [] (No. 1:25-cv-01991)). Zulkifli bin Hir aka “Marwan” was indicted [] by the Justice Department in August 2007 for conspiracy and providing material support to terrorists: Zulkifli Abdhir, aka “Zulkifli Bin Abdul Hir, aka “Hulagu,” aka “Marwan,” age 41, a fugitive believed to be in the Philippines, is charged in the indictment with conspiracy to provide material support to terrorists and providing material support to terrorists. In September 2003, the U.S. government designated Abdhir as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist pursuant to Executive Order 13224. In March 2007, the State Department added him to the most-wanted list of its Rewards for Justice program and authorized a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest or conviction ... In January 2015, Zulkifli bin Hir reportedly was killed [] during a raid by the Philippine National Police Special Action Force. Forty-four members of the police’s elite force also died in the assault. A finger taken from a man killed in the raid was delivered to the FBI for DNA analysis. The FBI stated [ “After a thorough review of forensic data and information obtained from our Philippine law enforcement partners, the FBI has assessed that terrorism subject, Zulkifli Abdhir ... is deceased and has been removed from the FBI’s list of Most Wanted Terrorists.” We sued after the FBI failed to respond to an April 25, 2025, FOIA request for records on Zulkifli bin Hir (aka “Marwan”) and his death during Oplan (Operation Plan) Exodus on January 25, 2015, in Mamasapano, Maguindanao, Philippines. The request asked for records about the collection, analysis, and chain of custody of a severed left index finger alleged to belong to Marwan, as well as photographs of his body and any related identification or forensic documentation. Marwan was a high-profile international terrorist on the FBI’s Most Wanted list with a $5 million reward. The operation that brought him down over a decade ago was a major event in Philippine and U.S. counterterrorism history. It’s time for transparency. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FOR RECORDS ON WORKPLACE INCIDENT INVOLVING ATTORNEY We’re in court to help a patent attorney get the records she rightfully deserves. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] on behalf of patent attorney Regina Ciolek against the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) for records concerning a reported “workplace incident” at the Broad Institute [] of MIT and Harvard (Regina Ciolek v. U.S. Department of Health and Human Services [] (No.1:25-cv-02764)). Ciolek [] worked as associate intellectual property counsel at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard from December 2016 to July 2021, where she was responsible for managing intellectual property matters and patent law. The Broad Institute receives funding from the National Institutes of Health, a component of Health and Human Services. Ciolek [] has over 20 years of experience in intellectual property law, specializing in biotechnology and life sciences. She holds a juris doctorate degree from Suffolk University Law School and a master’s in biology from Brandeis University. We sued in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia after the National Institutes of Health failed to respond to an April 16, 2025, request for: Copies of all records in NIH’s possession related to a workplace incident that occurred between December 2016 and present, where [Ciolek] was the victim. Specifically, [Ciolek] seek[s]: Any NIH reports, internal investigations, complaints, or communications (emails, memos, or reports) regarding this incident involving Sahand Hormoz, Nir Hacohen, and [Corri] Hale. Records of any disciplinary actions or safety measures taken as a result of the incident. Security reports or footage logs from NIH security personnel and/or Broad Institute personnel if they exist. * Records and/or images, in any way relating to trafficked non-consensual pornography of the victim, [Ciolek]. The three individuals connected to the incident named in our complaint are: Sahand Hormoz [], an associate professor of systems biology at Harvard University and associate professor of data science at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, with affiliations to the Broad Institute. Nir Hacohen [], a core institute member and the director of the Center for Cell Circuits at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard. He is the director of cancer immunology at the Mass General Hospital Krantz Family Center for Cancer Research, the David P. Ryan Chair in Cancer Research at the Mass General Cancer Center, and a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School. Cori (Corri) Hale [], senior counsel at the Broad Institute and previously an attorney at Hale Law PC, which specializes in the defense of medical professionals and research scientists, criminal law and business disputes. It is ridiculous that our client must resort to suing the government to obtain information that she is legally entitled to receive. Our lawsuits on behalf of clients challenging government actions are extensive. Most recently, we announced that the U.S. Air Force will finally provide full military funeral honors [] to Ashli Babbitt, the Air Force veteran who was shot and killed inside the U.S. Capitol by then-Capitol Police Lt. Michael Byrd on January 6, 2021. Babbitt was the only official January 6 homicide victim. The Biden administration had previously denied Babbitt and her family these honors in retaliation for being at the U.S. Capitol that day. This decision came on the heels of a massive, nearly $5 million Trump administration settlement to her family for wrongful death and other claims against the U.S. Government. In July 2025, the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court ruled [] that Bucks County, Pennsylvania acted in bad faith in unlawfully suppressing public records concerning the county health department’s Covid-19 school guidance. The Commonwealth Court affirmed the trial court’s [] May 2023 award of sanctions against Bucks County in the amount of $3,000 to Judicial Watch client Megan Brock. In January 2024, the City of San Francisco, in a 7-3 vote by the Board of Supervisors of the City and County of San Francisco, authorized a settlement agreement [] in a taxpayer lawsuit we brought against the city, agreeing to discontinue its discriminatory guaranteed-income program funded by taxpayer money in favor of transgender individuals with a preference for biological black and Latino men who identify as women. The agreement committed the city to pay $3,250 in attorney’s fees and costs and not to create a new guaranteed income program with the same eligibility criteria. HUD TO FINALLY STOP ILLEGALS FROM ‘RIDING THE COATTAILS OF AMERICAN TAXPAYERS’ Your tax dollars have been used to pay for the housing of thousands of illegal aliens, which means people who are legally present in the U.S. are deprived of help. Our Corruption Chronicles blog reports [ Earlier this year, in an effort to reverse the damage amid a nationwide affordable housing crisis, HUD and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) signed a Memorandum of Understanding [] [) to end the wasteful misappropriation of taxpayer dollars to benefit illegal aliens instead of American citizens, especially veterans in need. Under the agreement HUD provided a full-time staff member to assist in operations at the Incident Command Center (ICC), creating an interagency partnership to facilitate data sharing and ensure taxpayer-funded housing programs are not used to harbor or benefit illegal aliens. “We will safeguard precious taxpayer resources, and we will stop the harmful practices of the former Biden Administration, which favored and prioritized illegal aliens over American citizens in the expenditure of housing funds and subsidies,” the HUD-DHS MOU states. Within days HUD announced [] that illegal immigrants would no longer qualify for government-backed mortgages through a Federal Housing Administration (FHA) program that lends to “non-permanent residents.” The new policy ensures that illegal aliens cannot access FHA-insured financing and refocuses the use of taxpayer-funded federal housing programs to benefit U.S. citizens. A few days ago, HUD Secretary Scott Turner took another critical step, sending a letter [] [ over 3,000 Public Housing Authorities (PHA) around the nation requiring citizenship information for residents of the Section 8 program, which is funded by HUD and managed by local PHAs. Illegal aliens are not supposed to benefit from Section 8 housing, but enforcement has been lax for years and an estimated 100,000 non-citizens receive the taxpayer-funded subsidies. The audit will help clear the rolls and free resources to prioritize the needs of American citizens, according to Turner. PHAs have 30 days to provide tenant names, addresses, unit size and cost, number of people per unit and proof of American citizenship or eligible immigration status. “This information is required by law and this administration is upholding the law to its fullest extent,” Turner, a former Texas state legislator and professional football player, writes in the letter. “No longer will illegal aliens be able to leave citizenship boxes blank or take advantage of HUD-funded housing, riding the coattails of hardworking American taxpayers.” The nation’s housing secretary goes on to reveal that his agency currently serves only one out of four eligible families due in part to the lack of enforcement of prohibition against federally funded assistance to illegal aliens. “HUD will leverage all available enforcement actions against entities who do not comply with the request for citizenship information, including but not limited to, examination of HUD funding and/or evaluation of PHA program eligibility,” Scott’s letter to the country’s PHAs states. Public housing advocates claim the crackdown will destabilize poor families and worsen the nation’s housing crisis. “No matter where we come from, how long we’ve lived here, or what language we speak, our country has the resources to ensure that all of us have a safe place to call home,” said an official with the National Housing Law Project [], a nonprofit dedicated to advancing housing justice for poor people. “But Trump and Turner are threatening to take away the funding necessary to keep millions of people housed, despite tenants across the country struggling to make ends meet. Rather than address sky-high rents, increasing evictions, and record homelessness, Trump and Turner are forcing public housing authorities to divert their limited resources away from affordable housing and towards wasteful policy designed to cause fear and hardship among immigrant families and scare them into self-evicting.” Until next week, [Contribute] [] [advertisement] [] [32x32x1] [] [32x32x2] [] [32x32x3] [] [32x32x3] [] Judicial Watch, Inc. 425 3rd St Sw Ste 800 Washington, DC 20024 202.646.5172 © 2017 - 2025, All Rights Reserved Manage Email Subscriptions [] |
